Актуальный контроль индустрий ведётся скриптом по телам кейсов при планировании партии, а не по этому списку. --- ## Naive-error типы — покрытие (#1–#44) | Тип | Использован в | Раз | |---|---|---| | #1 historical-vs-replacement | 10, 25 | 2 | | #2 mix effect | 2, 5, 9, 22, **42** | 5 | | #3 flat-vs-escalating / обязательство | 4, 8, 14, 31, **33** | 5 | | #4 gross-vs-net | 7, 9, 32 | 3 | | #5 realized-vs-lifetime / фикс-vs-пер | 5, 15, 24, **38** | 4 | | #6 capacity | 3, 21 | 2 | | #7 unit mismatch / avg-vs-marginal | **12**, 19, 26, **36** | **4** | | #8 wrong criterion | 1, 6, 15, 29 | 4 | | **#9 корреляция vs причинность** | 11, 17, **35**, **44** | **4** | | #10 каннибализация | 4, 7, 28 | 3 | | #11 expected value / unit-econ | 13, 22, **37** | 3 | | #12 реакция конкурента / survivorship | 3, 27, **39** | 3 | | #13 локальная-vs-системная | 1, 23 | 2 | | #14 fixed-cost allocation / stranded cost | 12, 28, **41** | 3 | | #15 нерепрезентативная выборка | 2, 30 | 2 | **Тип #9 был использован 1 раз на 32** — приоритет закрыт: теперь **4 раза на 44**. --- ## Семь чеков точности (применены ко всем 44) **[1] Цепочка округления.** Считать точным путём (`Decimal`, не `float`), округлять **один раз в конце**. > **Дополнение после багов #33 и #34:** проверять на **каждом узле**, где округлённая величина показывается кандидату и затем входит в следующую формулу — **включая финальную сумму и сумму компонентов декомпозиции**. Расхождение «0.00 на одном звене» ≠ «0.00 на цепочке». > > **Частный случай (баг #34):** если кейс показывает компоненты **и** их тотал — компоненты обязаны складываться в показанный тотал **при той точности, с которой показаны**. −287 + (−143) = −430, а тотал −431 → лечится **добавлением знака**: −287.3 + (−143.4) = −430.7 → −431. > > **Универсальной точности показа НЕ существует.** #40 требует 2 знака, #42 — 3, #39 — 3. Точность выбирается **под числа конкретного кейса**, механической проверкой, а не правилом «показывай N знаков». **[2] Половина цента.** Числа на `.xx5` → `Decimal + ROUND_HALF_UP`. Годовые экстраполяции: `round(точное × 365)`, **не** `round(дневное) × 365`. **[3] База overstatement.** Наив сравнивается с **финальным Pyramid-числом**, не с промежуточным. **[4] Полный пересчёт в Sensitivity.** Если изменяемый вход проходит **внутри** многолетней цепочки (ramp/decay/эскалация/terminal) — пересчитывать всю цепочку, не приращением. Вход **снаружи** каскада (capex, разовое вычитание, порог) — приращение точно. **[5] Согласованность показанного.** Если величина **показана кандидату** округлённой — финал считается **от показанной версии**. Иначе кандидат, честно повторив расчёт, не сойдётся, и это выглядит как **его** ошибка. > Поймано в **#37** (утилизация 25.7447%, не 25.74% → $14,522), **#39** (эластичность 1.375, не 1.38 → $35,193), **#42** (contribution $13.776, не $13.78 → $628). **[5b] Одна сущность — одно число.** Порог/база/ставка не может иметь два значения в разных местах одного кейса. **[6] Единство метрики.** Сравниваемые как одна метрика величины считаются **одной формулой**. Формула выбирается из экономической логики **ДО просмотра результата**. > **Самый живучий баг библиотеки.** Пойман в **#33** (мультипликатор 7.5x для синергии vs DCF для обязательства) и повторён в **#36** (8x для naive/marginal vs DCF для финала). В **#41** применён превентивно: все денежные эффекты — perpetuity DCF @10%, мультипликатор не использован нигде. **[7] Текстовые правки при сборке.** Отдельно прогонять список **текстовых** правок, верифицируя по **наличию новых** формулировок, а не только по отсутствию старых чисел. > **Расширение на код (баг #33):** показанный кандидату Python-код — **тоже вывод Python**, а не иллюстрация. Копируется из прогона, не набирается руками по округлённым числам предыдущих шагов. > > **Расширение на прикидки (баг #36):** знак «≈» **не даёт индульгенции**. «≈$326M» оказался $334.1M — ошибка 2.4%. Прикидка в кейсе запрещена так же, как выдуманное число. ### 🔧 Мета-урок партии #33–#44 Баг **#34** — того же класса, что баг **#33**, и был написан **после** того, как урок #33 уже был зафиксирован в чек-листе. **Правило, записанное в документ, не применяется само.** Чек прогоняется по каждому кейсу **отдельно, механически** — а не «по памяти о том, что мы это уже проходили». Именно механический прогон поймал баг [1] в **#40** до ревью. ### 🔧 [8] СВОДНЫЕ ТАБЛИЦЫ — генерируются, а не пишутся **Три бага подряд, один корень.** Все три поймал ревьюер, и ни один не был в числах самих кейсов — все в **агрегатах**: | Баг | Механизм | |---|---| | #34 (компоненты) | сумма компонентов сложена в уме, не в Python | | Hard 15/17 → 12/20 | цифра перенесена из шапки, не сверена с registry | | Тип #7: 3 → 4 | таблица покрытия собрана вручную → **потерян один тег на кейсе с двойной маркировкой** (#12 = `#7+#14`) | **Правило.** Любая сводная таблица — difficulty, типы, покрытие naive-error, среднее время, доли — **генерируется скриптом из registry**, построчно. Не пишется руками, не переносится из предыдущей версии, не «дополняется» дельтой. **Особая опасность — кейсы с двойным тегом** (`#7+#14`, `#2+#5`, `#10+#3`). При ручной сборке один из двух тегов теряется молча, и grep по старым числам этого не видит. **Проверка перед отдачей:** реконструировать registry из текста и пересчитать **каждую** сводную цифру с нуля. Расхождение с заявленным — баг, независимо от того, насколько «очевидно» правильной выглядит записанная цифра. --- --- --- ---

steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass if ALL:** (1) counts port slots off the chart: **12** shoulder weeks × 1 slot = 12, plus **14** peak weeks at 1 slot every other week = **7**, total **19** calls — not 26; (2) names the binding constraint as the **Marquee Port slot**, not the **3,200** berths: real capacity is 19 × 3,200 = **60,800** berth-slots against **69,400** pax of demand, so demand **exceeds** capacity — the "83,200 berth-slots, room to spare" statement is wrong at the constraint; (3) uses the exhibit note — a sailing without the Marquee call **is not this product** — to rule out simply selling the 7 unserved weeks as an alternative itinerary.

**Fail if:** the candidate accepts 3,200 × 26 = 83,200 ≥ 69,400 and concludes demand fits; or counts the peak block as 14 slots (total 26) by missing "every other week"; or spots the shortfall but keeps sizing revenue off the full 69,400 demand.

steps.label: ГЛАВНЫЙ NUMERIC: COMBO  (5 min)
steps.candidate_md: ### 🔗 Число **с графика** × число **из таблицы** — в одной формуле
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
# CHART: how many sailings can actually dock?
shoulder = 12 weeks x 1 slot        # = 12
peak     = 14 weeks / 2             # = 7   (1 slot every OTHER week)
slots    = 12 + 7                   # = 19  sailings, NOT 26

# TABLE: berths per sailing
naive_capacity   = 3_200 * 26       # = 83,200 berth-slots
real_capacity    = 3_200 * 19       # = 60,800 berth-slots
```

**Реальная мощность 60,800 против наивных 83,200 — на 26.9% меньше.**
**Спрос 69,400 > 60,800 → пассажиров придётся рационировать.**

### 🔻 NAIVE — спрос помещается, берём всех

```python
naive_cm = 9_800*2_680 + 31_200*1_660 + 28_400*930   # = $104,468,000
naive_profit = 104_468_000 - 84_000_000              # = $ 20,468,000
naive_npv = sum(20_468_000/1.11**n for n in 1..8) - 96_000_000
# = +$9,330,841  ->  ENTER
```

### ✅ CORRECT — заполняем 60,800 по убыванию CM/pax

| Segment | CM/pax | Взято | Из спроса | CM |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Premium suite | $2,680 | 9,800 | 9,800 | $26,264,000 |
| Balcony | $1,660 | 31,200 | 31,200 | $51,792,000 |
| **Interior** | $930 | **19,800** | 28,400 | $18,414,000 |
| **Total** | | **60,800** | | **$96,470,000** |

```python
correct_profit = 96_470_000 - 84_000_000             # = $12,470,000
correct_npv = sum(12_470_000/1.11**n for n in 1..8) - 96_000_000
# = -$31,827,849  ->  DO NOT ENTER
```

### ⛔ **ФЛИП: NPV +$9,330,841 → −$31,827,849**

| | Naive | Correct |
|---|---|---|
| Capacity | 83,200 | **60,800** |
| Annual CM | $104,468,000 | $96,470,000 |
| **NPV** | **+$9,330,841** | **−$31,827,849** |
| Решение | Заходить | **Не заходить** |
| **Завышение** | | **129.32%** |

---

steps.label: Explain  (2 min)
steps.candidate_md:
**Q:** *The ship didn't get smaller. Why did capacity fall 27%?*

Мощность круизного маршрута — **не свойство судна**. Это минимум из: коек × рейсов, и **слотов в порту захода**. Судно может выйти в море 26 раз, но если причал Marquee Port принимает его 19 раз, а без Marquee Port это **другой продукт**, то рейсов ровно 19.

Ограничение — **не то, чем мы владеем**, а то, что нам выделяют. И оно жёстче в пик, ровно тогда, когда спрос максимален.

---
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass if ALL:** (1) states that capacity is a **minimum of two constraints**, not a property of the ship — berths × sailings **and** port slots at the call; (2) uses the slot arithmetic: the ship could sail **26** times but Marquee Port berths it **19** times (**12** shoulder weeks × 1 slot + **14** peak weeks at 1 slot every other week = **7**), and without Marquee Port it is a different itinerary, so 19 is the binding number — hence **3,200 berths × 19**, not × 26; (3) says the constraint is an **allocated** resource, not an owned one, and that it bites hardest **in peak**, exactly when the 69,400 passengers of demand is concentrated.

**Fail if:** the candidate explains the 27% drop by anything about the vessel (smaller ship, load factor, cabin mix, maintenance) or treats the port slots as a negotiable operating detail rather than the capacity ceiling that replaces 26 sailings with 19.

steps.label: ТВИСТ: сократить заходы?  (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: Коммерческий директор: *«Interior приносит всего $930. Уберём его — оставим Premium и Balcony, маржа вырастет»*.
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
# Only Premium + Balcony = 41,000 pax, needs ceil(41,000/3,200) = 13 sailings
premium_only_cm = 9_800*2_680 + 31_200*1_660        # = $78,056,000
# But fixed cost does NOT scale down 19 -> 13 sailings:
# crew, charter, port fees are seasonal, not per-sailing. Only fuel scales (~18% of fixed).
fixed_reduced = 84_000_000 * (1 - 0.18*(6/19))      # = $79,224,000
profit = 78_056_000 - 79_224_000                     # = -$1,168,000
```

**Отказ от Interior делает сезон убыточным.** Interior — 19,800 пассажиров, дающих $18.4M contribution против почти неизменного фикса.

💡 И глубже: **Interior — это заполняемость**. Круизная экономика построена на onboard spend, а он линеен по головам. Пустая каюта не тратит.

---

steps.label: Sensitivity  (3 min)
steps.candidate_md:
Атакует **A1 — распределение слотов в пиковые недели**.

> *«Порт предлагает гарантированный слот каждую пиковую неделю за $340,000 доплаты за заход. Переворачивает ли это вывод?»*

⚠️ Полный пересчёт: слоты **внутри** каскада.
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
slots = 12 + 14                                      # = 26  (full schedule)
capacity = 3_200 * 26                                # = 83,200 -> all demand fits
cm = 104_468_000
extra_fee = 340_000 * 7                              # = $2,380,000  (7 additional peak calls)
profit = 104_468_000 - 84_000_000 - 2_380_000        # = $18,088,000
npv = sum(18_088_000/1.11**n for n in 1..8) - 96_000_000
# = -$2,916,932   ->  STILL DO NOT ENTER
```

**Меняет цифру, не решение.** Разрыв сокращается с −$31.8M до −$2.9M — но проект остаётся отрицательным. Слоты можно **докупить**, и это почти спасает сделку.

```python
# Breakeven fee per additional peak call: NPV = 0
annuity_factor  = sum(1/1.11**n for n in 1..8)       # = 5.146123
required_profit = 96_000_000 / 5.146123              # = $18,654,821.20
breakeven_fee   = (104_468_000 - 84_000_000 - 18_654_821.20) / 7
# = $259,025.54 per call
```

Настоящий вывод sensitivity: **порог — $259,025.54 за заход**, а порт просит $340,000. Переговоры должны идти именно об этой цифре, а не о «доступе в принципе».

---

steps.label: Brainstorm (4 мин) + Синтез  (4 min)
steps.candidate_md:
**Как войти на маршрут, не покупая мощность, которой нет?**

*Продукт:*
1. Перепроектировать маршрут вокруг **второго** якорного порта, где слотов больше
2. Shoulder-сезонный продукт: 12 недель гарантированных слотов, короче сезон — ниже фикс

*Коммерция:*
3. Докупить пиковые слоты при цене ниже **$259,026/заход** (порог из sensitivity; порт просит $340,000)
4. Меньшее судно (2,000 коек) — фикс ниже, 19 рейсов заполняются полностью

*Структура:*
5. Alliance/slot-swap с оператором, у которого слоты есть, а спроса нет
6. Не заходить: NPV отрицателен, и это допустимый ответ

### Partner-level Pyramid
steps.interviewer_md:
> **We recommend Carnivia does not enter the Adriatic itinerary as structured — the NPV is minus $32 million, not plus $9 million.**
>
> Three facts. First, the binding constraint is not the ship, it is the port: Marquee Port allocates Carnivia one slot per shoulder week and one every other peak week, which is **19 sailings, not 26** — and without the Marquee call this is not the product we are selling. Second, that cuts capacity from 83,200 berths to **60,800**, against 69,400 of demand — we would turn away 8,600 passengers, all from Interior, the segment that carries onboard spend. Third, annual contribution falls from $104.5 million to $96.5 million against a fixed cost of $84 million, and eight seasons at 11% do not recover $96 million of capex.
>
> **We are being asked to buy a ship's worth of capacity for a port's worth of access.**
>
> Two risks. Internally, the instinct will be to drop Interior and "focus on margin" — that makes the season *loss-making*, because fixed cost is seasonal, not per-sailing, and Interior is 19,800 passengers of onboard spend. Externally, slot allocation is renegotiated annually and we would enter as the junior party: the incumbents who hold the peak weeks have every reason to keep holding them.
>
> Next steps. Within 45 days, open a slot negotiation with the port and establish the price of a guaranteed peak call — our breakeven is **$259,026 per call** against their asking price of $340,000, and above that threshold the itinerary does not work at any volume. In parallel, model the same product on a 2,000-berth vessel: nineteen sailings that fill completely beat twenty-six that cannot dock.

---

cases.title: Vendessa Tested Its Best 40 Machines
cases.header_md:
## Case 46 — Vendessa Tested Its Best 40 Machines

> **ПЛАШКА** 
> **Тип:** Profitability · **Индустрия:** Вендинг · **Формат:** F5  
> **Difficulty:** 🟢 Easy · **Depth:** ○ LIGHT · **Соответствие:** OK  
> **T/C:** Trap · **Naive:** #15 · **Время:** ~22 min

> **Reveal:** auto
> **optimal_entry:** 2  
>  
> **Слои insight:** ① F5 противоречие → нерепрезентативная выборка

**Profitability · Вендинг · Easy · Trap · ~22 min · naive #15 · gen B**
*Registry: Vendessa*

| Поле | Значение |
|---|---|
| № | 46 · **Vendessa** *(прототип: Selecta / Vendo)* |
| Индустрия | Вендинг |
| Тип | **Profitability** |

---
cases.prompt_md:
> **Vendessa** operates **8,600** vending machines. It piloted a "smart" machine — cashless payment plus telemetry — in **40 locations**.
>
> The pilot delivered **$271 per machine per month** in gross profit, against a fleet average of **$123**.
>
> Upgrade cost: **$1,180 per machine**. The CFO wants to roll out to the entire estate.
>
> **Should Vendessa?**

---

exhibits.title: Vendessa estate
exhibits.body_md:
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Office towers** | **11%** | 4,200 | $2.85 | **+1.4** |
| Transit hubs | 19% | 6,800 | $2.10 | +0.9 |
| Hospitals | 14% | 3,900 | $2.45 | +0.8 |
| **Factories** | **28%** | 2,100 | $1.90 | **+0.2** |
| Retail / other | 28% | 1,400 | $2.20 | +0.3 |

*Base vend conversion: 4.0% of footfall. Gross margin: 42%.*
*Pilot footnote: **all 40 pilot machines were sited in office towers**.*
*Cashless lift is driven by card penetration at the site — where cash is the norm, removing cash friction achieves little.*

**Q:** *Read the footnote and the lift column together. What is wrong with this pilot?*

📖 Пилот стоял в **офисных башнях — 11% парка** — и это **лучший** тип локации по обоим измерениям: высокий чек **и** максимальный cashless-lift (карты там уже норма). Заводы — **28% парка** — дают lift 0.2 пп: там платят наличными, и убирать «трение безнала» нечего.

---

steps.label: Framework  (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: Before we touch any numbers — how would you structure this decision? Talk me through your approach.
steps.interviewer_md:
Ожидается: **ROI = uplift × machines × 12 − upgrade cost**. И — критично — вопрос: *«где стояли эти 40 машин?»*

---

steps.label: F5: противоречие  (4 min)
steps.candidate_md:
**EXHIBIT A — Vendessa estate**

| Location type | Share of estate | Monthly footfall | Spend/vend | **Cashless lift (pp)** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Office towers** | **11%** | 4,200 | $2.85 | **+1.4** |
| Transit hubs | 19% | 6,800 | $2.10 | +0.9 |
| Hospitals | 14% | 3,900 | $2.45 | +0.8 |
| **Factories** | **28%** | 2,100 | $1.90 | **+0.2** |
| Retail / other | 28% | 1,400 | $2.20 | +0.3 |

*Base vend conversion: 4.0% of footfall. Gross margin: 42%.*
*Pilot footnote: **all 40 pilot machines were sited in office towers**.*
*Cashless lift is driven by card penetration at the site — where cash is the norm, removing cash friction achieves little.*

**Q:** *Read the footnote and the lift column together. What is wrong with this pilot?*

📖 Пилот стоял в **офисных башнях — 11% парка** — и это **лучший** тип локации по обоим измерениям: высокий чек **и** максимальный cashless-lift (карты там уже норма). Заводы — **28% парка** — дают lift 0.2 пп: там платят наличными, и убирать «трение безнала» нечего.

---
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass if ALL:** (1) names the selection problem explicitly — all **40** pilot machines sat in **office towers**, which are **11%** of the estate, so the pilot measured the best-case location, not the fleet; (2) shows office towers are best on **both** dimensions at once: highest footfall (**4,200**) and highest spend/vend (**$2.85**) give the largest base, and the highest cashless lift (**+1.4 pp**) gives the largest uplift — the two compound; (3) contrasts with **factories**, **28%** of the estate, at **+0.2 pp** lift, and gives the mechanism from the footnote: lift comes from card penetration, so where cash is the norm removing cash friction achieves almost nothing; (4) states the direction of the error — the fleet-weighted uplift must come out far below the pilot's **$271 vs $123** gap, so the **$1,180** upgrade cannot be justified off the pilot number.

**Fail if:** the $271 − $123 = $148 gap is carried to the whole **8,600**-machine estate; or the pilot is criticised only as "small sample, only 40 machines" or "needs a longer run" without naming that the sample is 100% office towers and that the lift column varies by location.

steps.label: ГЛАВНЫЙ NUMERIC  (5 min)
steps.candidate_md: Work out the gross-profit uplift per machine per month for each location type, and then the fleet-weighted uplift. Carry the decimals rather than rounding as you go.
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
# GP/machine/month = footfall x conversion x spend x margin
# Uplift = footfall x lift_pp x spend x margin   (exact, not rounded)
```

| Location | Legacy GP | Smart GP | **Uplift** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Office towers | $201.10 | $271.48 | **$70.3836** |
| Transit hubs | $239.90 | $323.87 | $53.9784 |
| Hospitals | $160.52 | $216.71 | $32.1048 |
| Factories | $67.03 | $90.49 | **$3.3516** |
| Retail / other | $51.74 | $69.85 | **$3.8808** |
| **Fleet-weighted** | **$123.43** | **$147.95** | **$24.5178** |

⚠️ **Uplift показываем с 4 знаками.** При округлении до $70.38 / $24.52 итоговый NPV уезжает на **$1,339** и **$805** — кандидат, честно повторив расчёт, не сойдётся.

### 🔻 NAIVE — перенести пилотный uplift на весь парк

```python
naive_uplift = 70.3836        # office tower uplift, EXACT
naive_annual = 70.3836 * 12 * 8_600          # = $7,263,587.52
rollout_cost = 1_180 * 8_600                  # = $10,148,000
naive_npv = sum(7_263_216/1.12**n for n in 1..5) - 10_148_000
# = +$16,035,607  ->  ROLL OUT
```

### ✅ CORRECT — uplift по фактическому миксу локаций

```python
correct_uplift = 24.5178      # fleet-weighted, EXACT
correct_annual = 24.5178 * 12 * 8_600        # = $2,530,236.96
correct_npv = sum(2_530_464/1.12**n for n in 1..5) - 10_148_000
# = -$1,027,049  ->  DO NOT ROLL OUT
```

### ⛔ **ФЛИП: NPV +$16,035,607 → −$1,027,049**

| | Naive | Correct |
|---|---|---|
| Uplift/machine/month | **$70.3836** | **$24.5178** |
| **NPV (5 лет @12%)** | **+$16,035,607** | **−$1,027,049** |
| Решение | Внедрять | **Не внедрять** |
| **Завышение** | | **1,661.33%** |

---

steps.label: Explain  (2 min)
steps.candidate_md:
**Q:** *The pilot was real. The machines really did make $271. Why is the number useless?*

Пилот измерил **не машину, а локацию**. Офисная башня даёт cashless-lift 1.4 пп, потому что там **карты уже в ходу** — smart-машина убирает реальное трение. На заводе платят наличными: lift 0.2 пп, убирать нечего.

Пилотные 40 машин стояли в **11% парка**, причём в лучших 11%. Заводы и ритейл — **56% парка** — дают uplift **$3.35–$3.88**, то есть в двадцать раз меньше.

📖 Выборка не была маленькой. Она была **не той**.

---
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass if ALL:** (1) states that the pilot measured the **location**, not the machine — **$271 per machine per month** is an office-tower number, and office towers are the best location type on both drivers (spend per vend and cashless lift), so the figure travels nowhere; (2) gives the mechanism, not just the observation: a smart machine only monetises friction that exists — office towers lift **1.4 pp** because card use is already near-total and the machine removes real friction, factories lift **0.2 pp** because people pay cash and there is nothing to remove; (3) quantifies the mismatch between where the pilot ran and where the estate is: the pilot sat in **11%** of the estate — the best **11%** — while factories and retail are **56%** of the estate and deliver uplift of **$3.35–$3.88**, roughly twenty times less; (4) implicitly or explicitly rejects the **$271** vs **$123** fleet-average gap as the uplift, since the two are measured on different location mixes.

**Fail if:** the candidate frames this as a small-sample or statistical-significance problem, or proposes simply running the pilot longer or on more machines — **40** was not too few; the sample was drawn from the wrong part of the estate, and more of the same locations would reproduce the same useless number.

steps.label: Синтез  (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: Vendessa's COO wants a go or no-go on the rollout. What's your recommendation?
steps.interviewer_md:
>
> Two facts. First, the pilot ran entirely in office towers, which are 11% of the estate and the single best location type on both drivers: highest spend per vend and highest cashless lift, because card penetration there is already near-total. Second, weighted across the actual estate the uplift is **$24.52 per machine per month, not $70.38** — factories and retail, which are 56% of the fleet, deliver under $4, because those sites run on cash and there is no friction to remove. On the true number, a full rollout returns minus $1 million.
>
> **The smart machine does not make money. Card penetration does.**
>
> Two risks. Internally, the estate has 8,600 machines and we know the location mix — this pilot could have been sited representatively for the same cost, and the fact that it was not suggests site selection is being driven by convenience rather than design. Externally, card penetration in factories is rising, and the answer changes when it does — this is a "not yet," not a "never."
>
> Next steps. Within 30 days, roll out to office towers, transit hubs and hospitals — 44% of the estate, where uplift runs $32 to $70 and the payback is under 24 months. In parallel, re-run the pilot in factories with a cash-and-card hybrid unit, because the question there is not whether telemetry works, it is whether anyone will tap a card.

---

**Partner answer (Pyramid):**

> **We recommend Vendessa does not roll out across the estate — but does roll out to 44% of it.**

cases.title: Corevault Can Afford the Campus. It Cannot Buy the Queue.
cases.header_md:
## Case 47 — Corevault Can Afford the Campus. It Cannot Buy the Queue.

> **ПЛАШКА** 
> **Тип:** Market Entry · **Индустрия:** Дата-центры · **Формат:** F6

cases.prompt_md:
> **Corevault** operates six data centres. It wants to enter a new metro with a **40 MW** campus.
>
> Finance built the budget from the last campus: **32 MW for $288 million** — **$9.0 million per MW**.
>
> Colocation pricing in the target metro: **$245 per kW per month**, stabilised utilisation **90%**, annual opex **$1.52 million per MW**. WACC **10%**.
>
> **Should Corevault enter?**

> 🔒 **F6.** Данные по репрайсингу компонентов и по подключению к сети **не выдаются**, пока кандидат их не запросит. Не спросил — считает по историческим костам и рекомендует сжечь $640M.

---

exhibits.title: memo от Head of Construction (prose)
exhibits.body_md:
> *The last campus was built **four years ago**. Component pricing has moved sharply, and not uniformly:*

| Component | Share of historical capex | **Price index now** |
|---|---|---|
| Shell & civils | 22% | 1.31x |
| **Power** (transformers, switchgear) | 28% | **2.15x** |
| Cooling | 19% | 1.68x |
| Racks & fit-out | 24% | 1.94x |
| Land | 7% | 1.45x |

exhibits.title: memo от Grid Liaison (prose)
exhibits.body_md:
> *The transmission operator's connection queue for loads above 30 MW currently runs **four years**. Position in the queue is by application date. It is **not transferable and not purchasable**.*
>
> *Capex is committed at FID. Revenue begins only at energisation.*

steps.label: Framework
steps.candidate_md: От чего зависит NPV площадки? Структурируй.
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass if ALL:** (1) NPV is split into an upfront capex leg and a recurring cash-flow leg discounted at **WACC 10%** — the cash-flow leg built as **40 MW** × **$245 per kW per month** × **90%** stabilised utilisation × 12, less opex of **$1.52 million per MW** — rather than a single "profitability" bucket; (2) the **$9.0 million per MW** figure is flagged as a benchmark to be tested, not an input: it is back-solved from the last campus (**32 MW for $288 million**) in a different metro, so power/grid interconnection, land, cooling and scale (40 MW vs 32 MW) must be checked before it is applied; (3) at least one bucket covers timing and durability of the revenue leg — how many years to lease up from zero to the **90%** stabilised level, contracted vs speculative capacity, and whether the **$245 per kW per month** rate holds at renewal or reprices; (4) a hypothesis is stated up front and the buckets are prioritised (which one, if wrong, kills the entry).

**Fail if:** the candidate treats **$9.0 million per MW** as the cost of the new campus and moves straight to arithmetic, or decides entry on the annual EBITDA margin alone with capex and the **10%** discount rate absent from the structure — Corevault's six existing sites make the per-MW benchmark feel safe, and that is exactly the assumption the case is built on.

steps.label: Промежуточный расчёт
steps.candidate_md: Work out what the 40 MW campus earns in a year, and what the numbers say about entering on Finance's budget.

steps.label: F6: кандидат должен спросить про косты  (4 min)
steps.candidate_md:
> 🔒 **Выдаётся только по запросу.**
>
> **EXHIBIT A — memo от Head of Construction (prose)**
>
> *The last campus was built **four years ago**. Component pricing has moved sharply, and not uniformly:*

| Component | Share of historical capex | **Price index now** |
|---|---|---|
| Shell & civils | 22% | 1.31x |
| **Power** (transformers, switchgear) | 28% | **2.15x** |
| Cooling | 19% | 1.68x |
| Racks & fit-out | 24% | 1.94x |
| Land | 7% | 1.45x |
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
weighted_index = 0.22*1.31 + 0.28*2.15 + 0.19*1.68 + 0.24*1.94 + 0.07*1.45
# = 1.7765     <- показываем 4 знака: при 1.78 capex уезжает на $1,260,000
replacement_per_MW = 9_000_000 * 1.7765             # = $15,988,500
```

⚠️ **Индекс показываем с 4 знаками.** При округлении до 1.78 стоимость 40 МВт завышается на **$1,260,000**.

**Replacement cost = $15.99M/MW против исторических $9.0M/MW.**

Питание подорожало **в 2.15 раза** — трансформаторы и распредустройства в дефиците из-за GPU-бума. Историческая себестоимость описывает кампус, который **уже нельзя построить по той цене**.

```python
replacement_capex = 40 * 15_988_500                 # = $639,540,000
npv_with_repl     = 45_040_000/0.10 - 639_540_000
# = -$189,140,000  ->  DO NOT ENTER
```

---

steps.label: ТВИСТ: F6, очередь на сеть  (5 min)
steps.candidate_md:
> 🔒 **Выдаётся только по запросу.**
>
> **EXHIBIT B — memo от Grid Liaison (prose)**
>
> *The transmission operator's connection queue for loads above 30 MW currently runs **four years**. Position in the queue is by application date. It is **not transferable and not purchasable**.*
>
> *Capex is committed at FID. Revenue begins only at energisation.*
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
# Capex spent now. Perpetuity of profit starts in year 5.
pv_delayed = (45_040_000 / 0.10) / 1.10**4          # = $307,629,260
correct    = 307_629_260 - 639_540_000
# = -$331,910,740  ->  DO NOT ENTER
```

### ⛔ **ФЛИП: NPV +$90,400,000 → −$331,910,740**

| Путь | NPV | Решение |
|---|---|---|
| **NAIVE** (historical cost, no queue) | **+$90,400,000** | Заходить |
| + replacement cost | −$189,140,000 | Не заходить |
| **+ 4-year queue = FINAL** | **−$331,910,740** | **Не заходить** |
| **Завышение** | **127.24%** | |

---

steps.label: Explain (2 мин): чего не купить за деньги  (2 min)
steps.candidate_md: **Q:** *Corevault has the capital. Why can't it just outspend the queue?*
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
# A competitor who applied 2 years ago energises in 2 years, not 4.
competitor_npv = (45_040_000/0.10)/1.10**2 - 639_540_000   # = -$267,308,595
value_of_2yr_head_start = -267_308_595 - (-331_910_740)    # = $64,602,145
```

**Позиция в очереди, взятая двумя годами раньше, стоит $64.6 миллиона.**

И её **нельзя купить**. Очередь — по дате заявки, не по цене. Конкурент, подавшийся в 2023-м, выйдет раньше нас независимо от того, сколько у нас капитала.

📖 **Партнёрский приём:** цифра говорит «дорого». Чего цифра не видит — **в этом бизнесе дефицитен не капитал, а время**, а время не торгуется.

---

steps.label: Sensitivity  (3 min)
steps.candidate_md:
Атакует **A2 — индекс замещения по питанию (2.15x)**.

> *«Дефицит трансформаторов рассасывается, индекс питания падает с 2.15 до 1.40. Переворачивает ли это вывод?»*

⚠️ Полный пересчёт: индекс **внутри** каскада.
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
new_index = 0.22*1.31 + 0.28*1.40 + 0.19*1.68 + 0.24*1.94 + 0.07*1.45
# = 1.5665
new_capex = 40 * 9_000_000 * 1.5665                 # = $563,940,000
npv = 307_629_260 - 563_940_000
# = -$256,310,740   ->  STILL DO NOT ENTER
```

**Меняет цифру, не решение.** Разрыв сокращается на $75.6M, но проект остаётся глубоко отрицательным — **потому что проблема не в цене оборудования, а в четырёх годах ожидания**. Даже бесплатный capex не спасёт актив, который не подключён.

**Настоящая точка чувствительности — очередь.** При очереди 0 лет и текущих костах NPV = **−$189M**; при очереди 4 года = **−$332M**. Очередь стоит **$143M**.

---

steps.label: Brainstorm
steps.candidate_md:
**Как войти, не покупая то, что не продаётся?**

*Обход очереди:*
1. Купить площадку **с уже полученным grid-подключением** — платим за очередь, а не за бетон
2. M&A: приобрести оператора, стоящего в очереди с 2023 года
3. Behind-the-meter генерация (газовые турбины + аккумуляторы) — не зависеть от сети

*Обход costs:*
4. Фазированная стройка: 15 МВт вместо 40 — под порог 30 МВт, где очередь короче
5. Закупить трансформаторы **сейчас** под будущую стройку — зафиксировать цену до дальнейшего роста

*Не входить:*
6. NPV отрицателен по всем сценариям — это допустимый ответ
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass: ≥5 ideas across ≥2 groups** — groups being (a) get the grid queue position instead of building it, (b) cut or re-shape the capex/build, (c) don't enter. At least **one** idea must attack the queue itself, not the concrete: buy a site that **already holds a grid connection**, M&A of an operator sitting in the queue **since 2023**, or **behind-the-meter** generation (turbines + storage) that removes dependence on the grid. Ideas must be labelled by group, not listed flat.

**Fail if:** every idea is a way to build the **40 MW** campus cheaper or faster (procurement, cheaper design, phasing alone) while the grid connection is still assumed purchasable on demand — that is the case's naive answer; or the candidate refuses to put **"do not enter"** on the list as a legitimate option; or fewer than 4 ideas after one push.

steps.label: Partner-level Pyramid
steps.candidate_md: Corevault's CEO has two minutes before the board. What's your recommendation?
steps.interviewer_md:
> **We recommend Corevault does not build in this metro — the NPV is minus $332 million, and the reason is not the money.**
>
> Three facts. First, the budget is built from a campus we constructed four years ago at $9.0 million per MW, but that campus can no longer be built at that price: power equipment has repriced 2.15x on the GPU shortage, and the weighted replacement cost is **$15.99 million per MW** — the capex is $640 million, not $360 million. Second, the grid connection queue for loads above 30 MW runs **four years**, and it is allocated by application date — it is not transferable and it cannot be bought. Capex is committed at FID; revenue begins at energisation. Third, discounting four years of delay against a $640 million commitment gives a present value of **minus $332 million**.
>
> **A competitor who joined the queue two years ago holds a $64.6 million asset that no amount of our capital can acquire.**
>
> Two risks. Internally, our budgeting convention anchors on historical build cost, and this is the second-largest capital decision in the pipeline — the same anchor is presumably distorting the others. Externally, the transformer shortage may ease, and we modelled it: even at a power index of 1.40 the NPV is minus $256 million, because the binding constraint was never the equipment.
>
> Next steps. Within 60 days, screen the market for sites with **existing grid connections** or for operators already holding queue positions — we should be buying time, not concrete. In parallel, model a 15 MW phased build, which sits below the 30 MW threshold where the queue is materially shorter; if the economics work at 15 MW, we enter small and grow into the position rather than waiting four years for a campus we cannot energise.

steps.label: Синтез
steps.candidate_md:
Сформулируй рекомендацию одной фразой и назови следующий шаг.

---
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass if ALL:** (1) leads with the verdict in one sentence, with an action verb — **"We recommend Corevault does not build the 40 MW campus in this metro"** — conclusion first, not built up to; (2) carries the number in that same sentence: NPV of **minus $332 million**, driven by the stale **$9.0 million per MW** benchmark taken from the 32 MW / $288 million campus, not by the revenue side ($245 per kW per month, 90% utilisation); (3) names one specific, ownable next step — re-baseline capex against a current-market quote per MW (power, land, shell) for this metro and re-run the NPV before the board decision — rather than a vague "do more analysis".

**Fail if:** the recommendation arrives after a recap of the analysis, or the next step is generic ("study the market further", "look at other metros") with no named input to re-baseline and no owner/decision point attached.

cases.prompt_md:
> **Agrikota Machinery** builds farm equipment. Average cost per unit rose from **$44,621 to $54,436** — up **22%** — while unit volume was flat (30,100 → 30,300).

> - **H1** — input inflation (steel, electronics)
> - **H2** — the product mix shifted toward complex machines
> - **H3** — plant productivity fell
>

---

exhibits.title: memo:
exhibits.body_md:
**H1 ОТВЕРГНУТА.** Рост по моделям — **3.3–3.8%**, то есть **ниже** blended-инфляции 4.3%. Agrikota абсорбирует инфляцию **лучше** рынка, а не хуже.

### ❌ H3 — упала производительность?

steps.candidate_md: How would you structure this? Give me your structure for why cost per unit moved, and for each of the CEO's three theories name the specific test that could prove it wrong.

Ожидается: разложить рост на **mix** и **rate**, и назвать **фальсифицируемый тест** под каждую гипотезу.

steps.label: Chart-reading  (3 min)
steps.candidate_md:
**EXHIBIT A — Agrikota by model**

| Model | Units Y1 | Units Y2 | Unit cost Y1 | Unit cost Y2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Compact tractor | 18,400 | 16,100 | $21,400 | $22,100 |
| Row-crop tractor | 9,600 | 10,900 | $58,200 | $60,400 |
| **Combine harvester** | **2,100** | **3,300** | **$186,000** | **$192,500** |
| **Total** | **30,100** | **30,300** | **$44,620.60** | **$54,436.30** |

**Q:** *Volume is flat. What changed?*

Комбайны выросли **в 1.57 раза** (2,100 → 3,300) — и стоят они **$192,500**, в 8.7 раза дороже компактного трактора.

steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass if ALL:** (1) checks each model's own unit cost and finds it moved only ≈ 3–4% ($21,400 → $22,100; $58,200 → $60,400; $186,000 → $192,500) — nowhere near the **22%** move in the total, so neither H1 (input inflation) nor H3 (productivity) can carry the gap; (2) identifies the mix shift: combine harvesters **2,100 → 3,300** at **$192,500** while compact tractors fall **18,400 → 16,100**, with total volume flat **30,100 → 30,300** — weight moved to the most expensive model; (3) states that "average cost per unit" is a **mix-weighted average**, so **H2** is the answer and the move must be split into a **mix** effect and a **rate** effect before any cost programme is designed.

**Fail if:** the candidate attributes the 22% to inflation or plant productivity, or launches a cost-reduction programme aimed at unit cost without separating mix from rate — cutting rate cannot recover a gap that mix created.


### 💡 **Тот же сдвиг микса поднял contribution на $378.9M (+23.5%)**

Себестоимость единицы выросла — **потому что Agrikota продаёт всё более дорогие машины**, и каждая из них приносит **$238,000** вместо $26,800.

📖 Кандидат, который «режет косты», атакует комбайны — самый прибыльный продукт компании.

---

steps.label: Sensitivity: **ОТКРЫТЫЙ ВОПРОС**  (3 min)
steps.candidate_md:
> *«Назови сам самое уязвимое допущение своего анализа. Изменит ли оно вывод — или только цифру?»*

Ожидаемый ответ: уязвимо **допущение, что микс — это выбор клиента, а не наш**. Я показал, что комбайны прибыльнее — но что если завод **не справляется** с их объёмом, и рост трудочасов в абсолюте (не на единицу) уже упирается в мощность?

**Но вывод не переворачивается.** Contribution per unit комбайна — **$238,000** против $26,800 у компактного трактора: даже при вдвое худшей утилизации комбайн выигрывает с запасом в **4.4 раза**.

⚠️ **Все варианты меняют цифру, не решение.** Кандидат, который здесь ищет разворот, **проваливает шаг**.

---
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass if ALL:** (1) volunteers a specific assumption of his own analysis, not a generic caveat — the strongest is that **mix is a customer choice rather than Agrikota's own constraint**: if the plant cannot absorb combine volume, absolute labour hours hit a capacity wall even though per-unit economics look good; (2) tests it against the numbers instead of asserting it — contribution per unit of **$238,000** for a combine against **$26,800** for a compact tractor, a cushion of about **4.4x**, so even materially worse utilisation leaves the combine ahead; (3) closes with the direction of the sensitivity: it **moves the number, not the decision** — the mix conclusion stands, and the board's cost-reduction programme is still the wrong response to a **22%** rise in average unit cost (from $44,621 to $54,436) on flat volume (30,100 → 30,300).

**Fail if:** the candidate hunts for an assumption that reverses the conclusion and claims to have found one, or offers a vulnerability with no quantification ("volumes could change", "steel prices are uncertain") — every available variant changes the figure only, and a claimed flip here is a failed step.

steps.label: Синтез  (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: > **The unit cost rise is a mix effect, and it is the best thing that happened to Agrikota this year — the board is about to launch a cost programme against its own most profitable product.**
steps.interviewer_md:
>
> Three facts. First, 81% of the $9,816 rise in average unit cost is mix: combine harvesters went from 7.0% to 10.9% of volume, and they cost $192,500 against $22,100 for a compact tractor. Second, inputs are **not** the problem — unit cost rose 3.3% to 3.8% per model against blended input inflation of 4.3%, meaning Agrikota is absorbing inflation better than the market. Third, productivity did not fall — labour hours per unit fell in every single model, by 3.2% to 4.8%.
>
> **And the mix that raised unit cost raised contribution by $378.9 million, or 23.5%.**
>
> Two risks. Internally, average unit cost is now a misleading KPI: it will keep rising as long as combines grow, and it will keep triggering cost programmes aimed at the wrong target. Externally, combines carry 8.7x the unit cost and 8.9x the contribution — the mix shift concentrates working capital and inventory risk in a product where a demand downturn hurts far more.
>
> Next steps. Within 30 days, retire blended unit cost as a board metric and replace it with contribution per unit and per production hour. In parallel, model the combine capacity constraint: at 3,300 units the line is running near design, and the real question is not how to cut cost but whether we can build more of the thing that makes $238,000 each.

---

steps.candidate_md: Work through what the CFO's proposal does to revenue, tenant type by tenant type, using the churn response in the exhibit. Give me the total and the picture underneath it.
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
# revenue = tenants x (1 - elasticity x 0.09) x fee x 1.09 x 12
```

| Type | Churn | Retained | New fee | New revenue | **Δ** |

| Tier-1 MNO | 1.62% | 4,131.96 | $2,376.20 | $117,820,360 | **+$7,948,360** |

### ✅ **Повышение работает: +$10,458,978 (+5.10%)**

Отток — **477 арендаторов из 10,100 (4.7%)**. Поскольку marginal cost ≈ $0, прирост выручки **есть** прирост прибыли.

### 🚨 Но **IoT теряет $490,965**

```python
breakeven_elasticity = (1 - 1/1.09) / 0.09          # = 0.9174
```

steps.label: F7: САМООПРОВЕРЖЕНИЕ  (4 min)
steps.candidate_md:
> **Q:** *You have just recommended a price rise worth $10 million. Before the CFO takes it to the board — what would have to be true for you to be wrong?*

Кандидат обязан **сам** назвать возражения. Три сильнейших:

### [1] Build-to-suit — Tier-2 построят свои вышки?
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
build_cost = $218,000 per tower;  annual_opex = $14,200;  WACC 9%
own_build_annualised = 14_200 + 218_000*0.09              # = $33,820/yr
own_build_monthly    = 33_820 / 12                        # = $2,818.33/month
our_new_Tier2_fee                                          # = $2,005.60/month
```
**Возражение НЕ ДЕРЖИТСЯ.** Собственная вышка стоит **$2,818/мес против нашей $2,006** — на 40% дороже. Строить невыгодно даже после повышения.

### [2] Консолидация MNO — слияние Tier-1 обрушит спрос?

```python
overlap = 14% of Tier-1 tenancies sit on towers where both merging parties are present
exposure = 117_820_360 * 0.14                             # = $16,494,850
```
**Возражение РЕАЛЬНО и КРУПНО** — $16.5M. Но: **вызывает ли его наше повышение?** Нет. Консолидация произойдёт независимо от цены. **Это риск бизнеса, а не аргумент против повышения.**

### [3] IoT — убиваем растущий сегмент?

```python
IoT revenue: $12,432,000 -> $11,941,035    # = -$490,965
IoT share of revenue: 6.06%
```
**Возражение ВЕРНО.** IoT — единственный сегмент с эластичностью **выше порога 0.92**, и он **теряет деньги**.

---

steps.label: CORRECT: сегментированное повышение  (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: Now compare the CFO's across-the-board increase with the best alternative you can build out of the tenant data. Which one produces more revenue, and by how much?
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
# OPTION A: raise everyone 9%
option_A = $215,706,978    # gain +$10,458,978

# OPTION B: raise everyone EXCEPT IoT
option_B = $216,197,943    # gain +$10,949,943
```

### ✅ **Option B выигрывает у Option A на $490,965**

| | Option A (всем) | **Option B (кроме IoT)** |
|---|---|---|
| Gain | +$10,458,978 | **+$10,949,943** |
| Решение | Повышать всем | **Повышать всем, кроме IoT** |

💡 **Расхождение с naive — 4.5%, без флипа направления.** Ответ «повышать» **верен**. Уточнение — **какому сегменту**.

📖 Это и есть содержание clean-кейса. Кандидат, натренированный на ловушках, будет искать разворот — и **найдёт три возражения**. Партнёрский уровень — **назвать их размер честно**: два не держатся, третье уточняет решение, но не отменяет его.

---

steps.label: Sensitivity  (3 min)
steps.candidate_md:
Атакует **A1 — эластичности из таблицы**.

> *«Эластичности — модельные оценки, не измерения. Что если Tier-1 на самом деле 0.55, а не 0.18?»*
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
# Tier-1 @ elasticity 0.55 instead of 0.18
churn   = 0.55 * 0.09                                     # = 4.95%
revenue = 4_200*(1-0.0495)*2_180*1.09*12                  # = $113,832,336.24
delta   = 113_832_336.24 - 109_872_000                    # = +$3,960,336.24  (was +$7,948,360.22)

# Option B (all except IoT), recomputed in full:
total_gain = 212_209_918.90 - 205_248_000                 # = +$6,961,918.90
```

**Меняет цифру, не решение.** Даже при утроенной эластичности Tier-1 повышение даёт **+$6,961,919** против +$10,949,943. Чтобы обнулиться, эластичность Tier-1 должна вырасти до **0.9174** — в **5.1 раза** против измеренной 0.18.

⚠️ **Все варианты меняют цифру, ни один не переворачивает.**

---

steps.label: Brainstorm (3 мин) + Синтез  (4 min)
steps.candidate_md:
**Как монетизировать IoT, не поднимая ему цену?**

*Ценообразование:*
1. Многолетний контракт со скидкой — фиксируем IoT, повышаем остальным
2. Tiered pricing по потребляемой мощности, а не по факту размещения

*Продукт:*
3. Продавать IoT edge-compute и backhaul — маржа без ценового давления
4. IoT как **loss-leader**: он заполняет вышки, где Tier-1 нет

*Портфель:*
5. Fixed wireless (эластичность 0.86) — впритык под порогом: повышать **осторожнее**, 5% вместо 9%

### Partner-level Pyramid
steps.interviewer_md:
> **We recommend Cellrell raises co-location fees 9% — on every segment except IoT, which is worth $10.9 million rather than $10.5 million.**
>
> Three facts. First, the marginal cost of a co-location tenant is effectively zero — the tower is a sunk asset — so every dollar of net revenue is a dollar of profit. Second, at 9% the blended churn is 4.7%, and the raise nets **$10.5 million** across all four segments. Third, the breakeven elasticity for a 9% rise is **0.92**, and IoT sits at 1.32 — it is the one segment where the raise **destroys** value, costing $490,965. Excluding it lifts the gain to $10.9 million.
>
> **We stress-tested three objections and none of them reverses the decision.** Build-to-suit does not hold: an own-built tower costs Tier-2 operators $2,818 a month against our post-raise $2,006. MNO consolidation is a real $16.5 million exposure — but it happens whether or not we raise prices, so it is not an argument against raising them. And IoT is real, which is why we are excluding it.
>
> Two risks. Internally, fixed wireless sits at elasticity 0.86 — just under the 0.92 threshold — so it clears by $144,000, which is thin; if the elasticity estimate is off by 8%, that segment flips too. Externally, the elasticities are modelled, not measured, and Tier-1 carries $118 million of revenue on an assumed 0.18 — that single number deserves a real test before we commit.
>
> Next steps. Within 30 days, run the raise on Tier-1 and Tier-2 at renewal and hold IoT flat. In parallel, measure actual churn response on the first 200 Tier-1 renewals before extending to fixed wireless, where the margin for error is $144,000 and the assumption is doing all the work.

---

steps.label: Декомпозиция вероятностей  (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: Given what you now know about the platform, work out for ALC-201 and ALC-330 the probability that the molecule succeeds conditional on the platform working. Then tell me what that does to each asset's overall probability of success.
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
P(platform OK) = 0.42

# Conditional molecule success, GIVEN the platform works:
P(201 molecule | platform OK) = 0.34 / 0.42 = 0.8095
P(330 molecule | platform OK) = 0.29 / 0.42 = 0.6905
```

⚠️ **Показываем 4 знака.** При 0.8095 и 0.6905 маргиналы восстанавливаются **точно**:
`0.42 × 0.8095 = 0.3400` ✅ · `0.42 × 0.6905 = 0.2900` ✅

### 💡 **Маргинальные вероятности НЕ ИЗМЕНИЛИСЬ.** ALC-201 по-прежнему 34%, ALC-330 по-прежнему 29%.

Изменилась только **совместная** вероятность.

---

steps.label: ГЛАВНЫЙ NUMERIC: сценарное дерево  (5 min)
steps.candidate_md: **Одна формула** — дерево сценариев, применённое к обоим случаям. Различается только структура зависимости.
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
# CORRECT: platform failure (58%) kills BOTH LipidCore assets
EV_correct = Σ P(scenario) × NPV(scenario)
           = $341.36M
```

### 🚨 **EV ИДЕНТИЧЕН. $341.36M в обоих случаях.**

Корреляция **не меняет ожидание**. Она меняет **распределение**.

| | Naive (independent) | **Correct (shared platform)** |
|---|---|---|
| **Expected value** | **$341.36M** | **$341.36M** ← идентично |
| **P(полный провал, $0)** | **27.65%** | **35.68%** |
| **P(сделка убыточна)** | 27.65% | **35.68%** |

```python
increase_in_wipeout_risk = 35.68 - 27.65        # = +8.03 pp
relative_increase        = 35.68/27.65 - 1      # = +29.04%
```

### ⛔ **Риск полного провала вырос на 29%. EV не сдвинулся ни на цент.**

---

steps.label: Explain  (2 min)
steps.candidate_md:
**Q:** *If the expected value is identical, why does the correlation matter at all?*

Потому что **компанию нельзя профинансировать средним**.

$341M — это среднее по сценариям, в **35.7%** из которых Alcybio получает **ноль** и списывает $240 миллионов. Наивная модель говорила: **27.7%**. Разница — **каждый двенадцатый сценарий**, переехавший из «что-то получилось» в «не получилось ничего».

📖 **Партнёрский приём:** цифра говорит «EV $341M > upfront $240M, берём». Чего цифра не видит — **два из трёх активов держатся на одной платформе**, и один провал Phase II выносит **68% портфеля** одним движением.

Диверсификация, за которую мы платим, **не куплена**. Мы купили один риск, обёрнутый в три названия.

---

steps.label: Sensitivity (3 мин) + Синтез  (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: ### Sensitivity — атакует **A1: P(platform) = 42%**
steps.interviewer_md:
> *«Что если LipidCore на самом деле надёжнее — 60%, а не 42%?»*

⚠️ Полный пересчёт: P(platform) **внутри** каскада — меняются все условные вероятности.

```python
P(platform) = 0.60
P(201 | platform) = 0.34/0.60 = 0.5667
P(330 | platform) = 0.29/0.60 = 0.4833
# marginals still 0.34 / 0.29 ✓

# WIPEOUT requires BOTH branches -- this is where it is easy to go wrong:
#   Branch 1: platform FAILS -> both LipidCore dead -> 455 must also fail
#   Branch 2: platform SURVIVES -> but both molecules fail anyway -> and 455 fails
branch_1 = (1-0.60) * (1-0.41)                        # = 23.6000%
branch_2 = 0.60 * (1-0.5667) * (1-0.4833) * (1-0.41)  # =  7.9256%
P(wipeout) = 31.5256%                                  # (vs 35.68% at platform 0.42)

EV = $341.36M                                          # unchanged, again
```

⚠️ **Ветвь 2 растёт в 5.4 раза** (1.46% → 7.93%) при более надёжной платформе: если платформа выживает **чаще**, то условная вероятность успеха молекулы **падает** (0.8095 → 0.5667), потому что маргинал зафиксирован на 34%. Забыть эту ветвь — значит недооценить хвост.

**Меняет хвост, не среднее — и не решение.** Даже при платформе 60% риск полного провала **31.53% против 27.65%** независимого случая. Концентрация никуда не делась, она лишь мельче.

**Настоящий вывод sensitivity:** EV **невосприимчив** к структуре зависимости. Любой анализ, который смотрит только на EV, **не увидит эту проблему ни при каком значении параметра**. Проблема не в числе — **в метрике**.

### Partner-level Pyramid

> **We recommend Alcybio does not in-license the portfolio at $240 million as structured — not because the expected value is wrong, but because it is the wrong number to decide on.**
>
> Three facts. First, the expected value is **$341 million against $240 million upfront**, and that is correct — we verified it. Second, ALC-201 and ALC-330 both run on the LipidCore delivery platform, which has a 42% chance of clearing Phase II; if it fails, **both assets fail together**, regardless of molecule. Third, and this is the point: correcting for that shared dependency leaves the expected value **completely unchanged at $341 million** — but the probability of walking away with **nothing** rises from 27.7% to **35.7%**, a 29% increase in wipeout risk.
>
> **We are not buying three shots on goal. We are buying one platform bet and a hedge.**
>
> Two risks. Internally, our valuation convention is expected value, and expected value is **structurally blind** to this — no value of any parameter would have surfaced it, which means every portfolio decision we have made on this basis carries unknown concentration. Externally, LipidCore is a third-party platform: if it fails in someone else's trial before ours reads out, both our assets are impaired before we ever dose a patient.
>
> Next steps. Within 30 days, restructure the deal — take ALC-455 and **one** LipidCore asset outright, and option the second contingent on the platform clearing Phase II; that converts a correlated bet into a sequential one at a fraction of the upfront. In parallel, re-run the last three portfolio decisions on a scenario basis rather than expected value, because this is unlikely to be the only place the metric has hidden a concentration we did not price.

---

Обе ветви теперь показаны явно ✅ | | [5] Согласованность показанного | **ПОЙМАНО.** Условные вероятности показываем с **4 знаками** (0.8095 / 0.6905) — тогда `0.42 × 0.8095 = 0.3400` восстанавливает маргинал **точно**. ---
cases.prompt_md:
> **Streakhouse** is launching a paid subscription for its esports streaming platform.
>
> Price: **$9.99/month**. Projected: **340,000 subscribers**.
>
> *"That's $40.8 million of revenue against $18.6 million of product cost. We launch."*
>
> **Do they?**

---

exhibits.title: Streakhouse subscription stack
exhibits.body_md:
|---|---|---|
| **App store commission** | **30%** | **70% of subs** *(mobile)* |
| Payment processing | 2.9% | 30% of subs *(web)* |
| **Creator revenue share** | **50%** | **of NET RECEIPTS** *(contractual)* |
| Annual product cost | **$18,600,000** | engineering, DRM, content ops, live infra |

**Q:** *All three fees are stated in the exhibit. Which of them did the $40.8 million figure account for?*

📖 **Ни одну.** $40,759,200 — это **gross bookings**, деньги, которые подписчики нажали в приложении. К Streakhouse они не приходят.

---

steps.label: Framework  (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: Take a minute or two and structure whether this subscription makes money for Streakhouse. Walk me through it.
steps.interviewer_md:
Ожидается: **прибыль = NET-выручка − фикс-косты**. И вопрос: *«что стоит между подписчиком, платящим $9.99, и деньгами на нашем счету?»*

🚩 Флаг, если кандидат берёт $9.99 × 340,000 × 12 как выручку Streakhouse.

---

steps.label: F5: противоречие  (4 min)
steps.candidate_md:
**EXHIBIT A — Streakhouse subscription stack**

| Item | Rate | Applies to |
|---|---|---|
| **App store commission** | **30%** | **70% of subs** *(mobile)* |
| Payment processing | 2.9% | 30% of subs *(web)* |
| **Creator revenue share** | **50%** | **of NET RECEIPTS** *(contractual)* |
| Annual product cost | **$18,600,000** | engineering, DRM, content ops, live infra |

**Q:** *All three fees are stated in the exhibit. Which of them did the $40.8 million figure account for?*

📖 **Ни одну.** $40,759,200 — это **gross bookings**, деньги, которые подписчики нажали в приложении. К Streakhouse они не приходят.

---

steps.label: ГЛАВНЫЙ NUMERIC  (5 min)
steps.candidate_md: ⚠️ **Порядок применения критичен.** App store берёт своё **первым** (с верха). Creator share — контрактно **с net receipts**, то есть **после** платформенных комиссий.

steps.label: Explain: сколько остаётся от $9.99  (2 min)
steps.candidate_md: Walk me down from what a subscriber pays to what Streakhouse actually keeps in hand. And on that number, how many subscribers does the business need to break even?
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
net_per_sub_per_month = 15_922_581.50 / 340_000 / 12 # = $3.90
keep_rate             = 15_922_581.50 / 40_759_200   # = 39.07%
```

| | |
|---|---|
| Подписчик платит | **$9.99** |
| App store забирает *(на 70% объёма)* | −$2.10 |
| Processing *(на 30%)* | −$0.09 |
| **Net receipts** | **$7.80** |
| **Creator share (50%)** | **−$3.90** |
| **Streakhouse оставляет** | **$3.90** |

### 💡 **Keep rate — 39%.** Из каждых $10 на счёт приходит меньше $4.

```python
breakeven_subs = 18_600_000 / (15_922_581.50/340_000) # = 397,172 subscribers
```

**Breakeven — 397,172 подписчика** против прогнозных 340,000. Нужно **на 16.8% больше**.

📖 **So-what:** ошибка не в прогнозе подписчиков. Ошибка в том, что бизнес-кейс построен на выручке, **которую Streakhouse никогда не увидит**.

---

steps.label: Синтез  (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: Streakhouse's CEO walks in and asks straight out: do we launch or not? Your recommendation.
steps.interviewer_md:
>
> Two facts. First, the $40.8 million figure is gross bookings, not revenue: the app store takes 30% on the 70% of subscribers who sign up on mobile, processing takes 2.9% on web, and the creator share is a contractual 50% of what remains. Streakhouse's actual net revenue is **$15.9 million**. Second, against $18.6 million of product cost that is a **$2.7 million loss**, and breakeven sits at **397,000 subscribers** — 17% above the projection.
>
> **Of every $9.99 a subscriber pays, Streakhouse keeps $3.90.**
>
> Two risks. Internally, the business case was built on a number that never reaches our bank account, and the same gross-versus-net error is likely sitting in the ad-tier and merchandise models. Externally, the creator share is contractual and the app store commission is not ours to negotiate — the only lever we actually control is the mobile-versus-web mix, and it currently runs 70/30 against us.
>
> Next steps. Within 30 days, model a web-first launch with in-app deep links: shifting the mix from 70/30 mobile to 40/60 web lifts net revenue by roughly $2.5 million and clears breakeven at the current subscriber projection. In parallel, reopen the creator agreement — a 50% share of net receipts is a co-ownership structure, not a revenue share, and the product cannot fund itself under it.

---

**Partner answer (Pyramid):**

> **We recommend Streakhouse does not launch at these economics — the product loses $2.7 million, it does not make $22 million.**

cases.prompt_md:
> **Castwell Forge** runs four furnaces. The plant manager wants to shut **Furnace D**:

---

exhibits.title: memo от Quality Director (prose)
exhibits.body_md:
>
> *Re-certifying Furnace A: **22 months**, and A's lining chemistry does not qualify without a full reline.*
>
> *Aerospace castings: **3,200 tonnes/yr** at **$11,400/tonne**, variable cost **$4,900/tonne** (ex-furnace). **All of it runs on D.***

```python
aerospace_CM = 3_200 * (11_400 - 4_900)       # = $20,800,000

correct = 3_526_000 - 20_800_000              # = -$17,274,000
```

### ⛔ **ФЛИП: +$3,526,000 экономии → −$17,274,000 убытка**

| | Naive | Correct |
|---|---|---|
| Avoided cost | $7,380,000 | $7,380,000 |
| Relocation | −$3,854,000 | −$3,854,000 |
| **Lost aerospace CM** | *(не учтён)* | **−$20,800,000** |
| **Итог** | **+$3,526,000** | **−$17,274,000** |
| Решение | Закрыть D | **Не закрывать** |
| **Завышение** | | **120.41%** |

---

steps.label: Framework  (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: How would you structure whether shutting Furnace D actually saves money? Take a minute.
steps.interviewer_md:
Ожидается: **экономия = избегаемый кост − стоимость переноса объёма − потерянный вклад**. И вопрос: *«почему D дороже? Что он делает такого, чего не делают остальные?»*

🚩 Флаг, если кандидат принимает $/тонна за меру эффективности, не спросив, **одинаковую ли тонну** производят печи.

---

steps.label: Промежуточный расчёт  (4 min)
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass if ALL:** (1) reads the last column as the point: **D is the only aerospace-certified furnace**, so its **4,100** tonnes cannot simply be moved to A/B/C — the certification, not the spare capacity, is the binding constraint; (2) reframes the **$1,800/t**: it is not inefficiency but the cost of running certified work, so cost per tonne across furnaces is not comparable and $1,800 vs $1,300 is not a like-for-like gap; (3) states what the decision actually requires — the contribution earned on the aerospace volume that would be lost against the **$7,380,000** of avoided annual cost, rather than the plant manager's **$3.5 million**; (4) flags that shutting D loses the certified capability (and likely the customer qualification behind it), not just the tonnage.

**Fail if:** the answer is that the **4,100** tonnes fit inside the **5,600** tonnes of spare capacity and therefore the ~**$3,526,000** saving stands; or the last column is read as "D should be made more efficient / get the others certified" without stopping the shutdown logic.

steps.label: ГЛАВНЫЙ NUMERIC  (5 min)
steps.candidate_md: ### 🔻 NAIVE — закрыть D, перенести объём

```python
# 4,100 t fits in 5,600 t of spare capacity ✓

naive_saving = 7_380_000 - 3_854_000          # = +$3,526,000  ->  SHUT IT
```

### ✅ CORRECT — D сертифицирована, остальные нет

**EXHIBIT B — memo от Quality Director (prose)**

> *Furnace D holds the only **AS9100 + NADCAP** certification for aerospace-grade alloy. Certification is granted **to the furnace**, not the company — it covers the specific lining chemistry and thermal profile.*
>
> *Re-certifying Furnace A: **22 months**, and A's lining chemistry does not qualify without a full reline.*
>
> *Aerospace castings: **3,200 tonnes/yr** at **$11,400/tonne**, variable cost **$4,900/tonne** (ex-furnace). **All of it runs on D.***

```python
aerospace_CM = 3_200 * (11_400 - 4_900)       # = $20,800,000

correct = 3_526_000 - 20_800_000              # = -$17,274,000
```

### ⛔ **ФЛИП: +$3,526,000 экономии → −$17,274,000 убытка**

| | Naive | Correct |
|---|---|---|
| Avoided cost | $7,380,000 | $7,380,000 |
| Relocation | −$3,854,000 | −$3,854,000 |
| **Lost aerospace CM** | *(не учтён)* | **−$20,800,000** |
| **Итог** | **+$3,526,000** | **−$17,274,000** |
| Решение | Закрыть D | **Не закрывать** |
| **Завышение** | | **120.41%** |

---

steps.label: Explain  (2 min)
steps.candidate_md:
**Q:** *Why is D more expensive per tonne?*

**Именно потому, что делает аэрокосмические отливки.** Малые партии, спецсплав, жёсткий термопрофиль, сертификационный аудит. $1,800/т — это **не неэффективность, это цена допуска**.

Метрика «$/тонна» предполагает, что все печи производят **одну и ту же тонну**. Они не производят. Тонна с печи D продаётся за **$11,400**, тонна с печей A/B/C — за рядовую цену.

📖 Сертификация выдана **печи**, а не компании. Закрыв D, Castwell не переносит производство — она **теряет право его вести**.

💡 **So-what:** самая «неэффективная» печь генерирует **$20.8M contribution** — почти половину всего годового коста завода.

---
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass if ALL:** (1) explains **$1,800 a tonne** as the price of admission rather than inefficiency, and names the physical reasons it is higher: small lots, special alloy, tight thermal profile, certification audit — D costs more **because** of what it makes, not despite it; (2) attacks the metric itself: **$/tonne** presumes every furnace produces the same tonne, and they do not — a tonne off D sells for **$11,400** while A/B/C tonnes sell at commodity price, so the **$1,800** vs **$1,300** comparison has no common denominator; (3) makes the so-what quantitative — the "worst" furnace generates **$20.8M** of contribution, close to half the plant's entire annual cost base; (4) notes that the certification attaches to the **furnace**, not to Castwell, so shutting D does not relocate the work — it forfeits the right to do it.

**Fail if:** the candidate defends D purely on fixed-cost absorption or overhead reallocation ("the $1,300 furnaces will look worse once D's overhead moves onto them") without touching product mix and price per tonne, or accepts the plant manager's **$3.5 million** saving as real and argues only that D's **$1,800** could be brought down through efficiency.

steps.label: Синтез  (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: Castwell's CEO is asking whether to go ahead with the furnace closure or not. Your recommendation.
steps.interviewer_md:
>
> Two facts. First, D is the only furnace holding AS9100 and NADCAP certification for aerospace-grade alloy, and that certification attaches to the **furnace**, not to Castwell — re-certifying Furnace A takes 22 months and requires a full reline its chemistry does not currently support. Second, the aerospace line runs **3,200 tonnes at $11,400 a tonne** against $4,900 of variable cost, generating **$20.8 million of contribution** — all of it on D. Shutting D does not relocate that production. It ends it.
>
> **D costs $1,800 a tonne because of what it makes, not despite it.**
>
> Two risks. Internally, cost per tonne is the plant's primary efficiency metric, and it is structurally blind to product mix — it assumes every furnace makes the same tonne, and D does not. This is unlikely to be the only decision it has distorted. Externally, aerospace certification is a barrier that took years to earn; if we surrender it, re-entry is a 22-month project and a customer-qualification cycle we may not win back.
>
> Next steps. Within 30 days, replace cost per tonne with contribution per tonne in plant reporting — D goes from worst furnace to the one generating $6,500 of contribution on every tonne it pours. In parallel, if capacity is genuinely the concern, the question is not whether to close D but whether to **certify a second furnace**, because we currently have a $20.8 million business running on a single point of failure.

---

**Partner answer (Pyramid):**

> **We recommend Castwell does not shut Furnace D — closing it would cost $17.3 million, not save $3.5 million.**

cases.title: Hoppily Ever After?
cases.header_md:
## Case 53 — Hoppily Ever After?

> **ПЛАШКА** 
> **Тип:** M&A · **Индустрия:** Пивоварение · **Формат:** F1  
> **Difficulty:** 🟡 Medium · **Depth:** 🔥 STRONG · **Соответствие:** ↑выше  
> **T/C:** Trap · **Naive:** #10 · **Время:** ~33 min  
> **Экспонаты (2):** table — consumer panel, n = 2,400 CraftHaven drinker; table — retail scanner, Brewhalla core regions, 24 м  
> **Reveal:** on_request
> **optimal_entry:** 3  
>  
> **Слои insight:** ① F1 панель потребителей ② скрытая корректировка: сканер-данные vs панель (конфликт источников)

**M&A · Пивоварение · Medium · Trap · ~33 min · naive #10 · gen B**
*Registry: Hoppily Ever After?*

| Поле | Значение |
|---|---|
| № | 53 · **Brewhalla** *(прототип: AB InBev / Carlsberg)* |
| Индустрия | Пивоварение |
| Грунтовка | **Kellogg p.231 Beverages** — brand equity, shelf space через market share, raw materials ~70% COGS |
| Тип | **M&A** |
| Difficulty | **Medium** |
| Trap/Clean | 🔴 Trap |
| Время | 33 мин · 9 шагов |
| Формат | **F1** — скрытая корректировка |
| Exhibit | Таблица + **bar-chart COMBO** (панель/сканер) |
| Naive-error | **#10 — каннибализация** |
| Твист | Панель говорит 36%, сканер — 54% |

---
cases.prompt_md:
> **Brewhalla** brews mainstream lager: **8.4 million hl/year** at a contribution of **$38/hl**.
>
> It has agreed heads of terms to acquire **CraftHaven**, a fast-growing craft brewery: **640,000 hl/year** at **$92/hl** contribution. Seller's ask: **$580 million**.
>
> The strategy deck: *"Craft is where the growth is. CraftHaven adds $58.9M of contribution — at our 9% cost of capital that is $654M of value against a $580M price."*
>
> **Should Brewhalla close?**

---

exhibits.title: consumer panel, n = 2,400 CraftHaven drinkers (self-reported
exhibits.body_md:
|---|---|
| Mainstream lager — Brewhalla brands | **36%** |
| Mainstream lager — other brands | 17% |
| Other craft | 21% |
| Wine / spirits / none | 26% |
| **Total** | **100%** |

Кандидат пересчитывает: для перебежчиков сделка захватывает только **разницу** CM (92 − 38), не полные 92 — их $38 Brewhalla уже зарабатывала до сделки.

---

exhibits.title: retail scanner, Brewhalla core regions, 24 мес (по запросу)

steps.label: Framework  (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: Take a minute and walk me through how you'd approach whether this acquisition is worth the ask.
steps.interviewer_md:
Ожидается: **ценность = инкрементальный CM / 0.09**, и — критично — вопрос: *«откуда CraftHaven берёт своих пьющих?»*

🚩 Флаг, если кандидат складывает CM двух компаний, не спросив о пересечении аудиторий.

---

steps.label: Naive  (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: Value CraftHaven off its contribution and tell me how that sits against the seller's ask.

steps.label: F1: панель потребителей  (4 min)
steps.candidate_md:
**EXHIBIT A — consumer panel, n = 2,400 CraftHaven drinkers (self-reported)**

| "Before CraftHaven I mostly drank…" | Share |
|---|---|
| Mainstream lager — Brewhalla brands | **36%** |
| Mainstream lager — other brands | 17% |
| Other craft | 21% |
| Wine / spirits / none | 26% |
| **Total** | **100%** |

Here's the consumer panel we ran on CraftHaven's drinkers. Before you calculate anything — what do you see in it, and what does it do to the deck's number?
steps.interviewer_md:
**Pass if ALL:** (1) reads that **36%** of CraftHaven's drinkers came off Brewhalla's own mainstream lager brands — the deal is partly buying back customers Brewhalla already had; (2) names the mechanism and reprices it: on those switchers the deal captures only the **difference** in contribution (**92 − 38**), not the full **92**, because Brewhalla was already earning **$38/hl** on them; (3) separates that from what is genuinely incremental — the 17% other-brand mainstream, 21% other craft and 26% wine/spirits/none — and flags that the panel is **self-reported**, so 36% is a floor, and asks for hard (non-recall) evidence.

**Fail if:** candidate values all **640,000 hl at the full $92** as incremental (the deck's $58.9M → $654M vs the $580M ask), or notes the 36% qualitatively as "some overlap" without repricing those volumes at 92 − 38.

steps.label: Скрытая корректировка: сканер-данные  (4 min)
steps.candidate_md:
**EXHIBIT B — retail scanner, Brewhalla core regions, 24 мес (по запросу)**

*Bar chart; оси: X = период (8 кварталов), Y = Δ объёма, тыс. hl/квартал. Данные графика:*

| Квартал | CraftHaven Δ, тыс. hl | Brewhalla SKUs Δ (те же магазины), тыс. hl |
|---|---|---|
| Q1 | +14.2 | −7.1 |
| Q2 | +16.8 | −8.9 |
| Q3 | +18.1 | −9.6 |
| Q4 | +19.4 | −10.8 |
| Q5 | +21.0 | −11.5 |
| Q6 | +22.6 | −12.4 |
| Q7 | +23.9 | −13.1 |
| Q8 | +25.3 | −13.6 |
| **Σ 24 мес** | **+161.3** | **−87.0** |
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
matched_share = 87.0 / 161.3        # = 53.94% ≈ 54%
```

📖 **Панель занижает: люди не признаются, что «изменили» бренду.** Сканер меряет полку, а не память. Каннибализация — **54%**, не 36%.

📖 **Панель занижает: люди не признаются, что "изменили" бренду.** Сканер меряет полку, а не память. Каннибализация — **54%**, не 36%.

---

steps.label: ГЛАВНЫЙ NUMERIC  (5 min)
steps.candidate_md: Value the deal: what incremental annual contribution does CraftHaven actually bring to the combined group once you account for where its volume comes from and for what happens to shelf space? Turn that into a value at the client's cost of capital and compare it with the ask.
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
new_drinkers = 640_000 * 0.46 * 92             # = $27,084,800
switchers    = 640_000 * 0.54 * (92 - 38)      # = $18,662,400
incremental  = 27_084_800 + 18_662_400         # = $45,747,200
```

**Плюс полка (грунтовка Kellogg: market share → shelf space):** ритейлеры ограничивают суммарные фейсинги объединённого портфеля — CraftHaven теряет **6%** объёма при ребалансировке к конкурентам.

```python
shelf_loss = 640_000 * 0.06 * 92               # = $3,532,800
correct_cm = 45_747_200 - 3_532_800            # = $42,214,400
correct_val = 42_214_400 / 0.09                # = $469,048,888.89
```

### ⛔ **ФЛИП: $654.2M → $469.0M против аска $580M**

| | Naive | Correct |
|---|---|---|
| Каннибализация | 0% | **54% (сканер)** |
| Годовой CM | $58,880,000 | **$42,214,400** |
| Ценность @9% | **$654,222,222** | **$469,048,889** |
| vs аск $580M | BUY (+$74.2M) | **WALK (−$110.95M)** |
| **Завышение** | | **39.48%** |

---

steps.label: Explain  (2 min)
steps.candidate_md:
**Q:** *The panel is a real survey of real drinkers. Why is the scanner right and the panel wrong?*

Панель спрашивает память и самоидентификацию; признаться «я ушёл с массового лагера» — значит признать, что ты был его аудиторией. Сканер видит **полку**: тот же магазин, тот же месяц, минус ящик Brewhalla — плюс ящик CraftHaven. Поведение против показаний.

---

steps.label: Sensitivity ([9]: Python)  (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: Атакует **A1 — сканерные 54%**: продавец будет оспаривать методологию. Полный пересчёт value(c):
steps.interviewer_md:
```python
def value(c):
    inc = 640_000*(1-c)*92 + 640_000*c*(92-38)
    return (inc - 3_532_800) / 0.09

value(0.36) = $517,688,888.89     # даже ПАНЕЛЬНАЯ цифра -> WALK
value(0.45) = $493,368,888.89
value(0.54) = $469,048,888.89
breakeven_cann = 0.1294           # verify: value(0.1294) = 580,000,000.00
```

### 💡 **Breakeven-каннибализация — 12.94%.** Даже если продавец прав и верна панель (36%), сделка при $580M разрушает $62.3M. Спор «панель vs сканер» **не меняет решение — он меняет контр-цену** ($518M vs $469M).

steps.label: Brainstorm  (4 min)
Синтез  (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: The investment committee is on the line and wants one answer: do we buy or walk? Your recommendation.
steps.interviewer_md:
>
> Three facts. First, retail scanner data shows **54%** of CraftHaven's growth in our core regions is matched store-by-store by decline in our own SKUs — the consumer panel's 36% is self-reported and understates switching. Second, for a switcher the deal captures only the contribution difference of $54 per hl, not the full $92 — we already earn $38 on that drinker. That cuts incremental contribution from $58.9 million to $45.7 million. Third, retailers cap combined facings: consolidation costs a further 6% of volume, landing at **$42.2 million of true incremental contribution — $469 million of value at our cost of capital.**
>
> **At $580 million we would pay a $111 million premium to buy back drinkers we already own.**
>
> Two risks. Internally, the panel-based cannibalization figure is used across our innovation pipeline, and every line extension case built on it is overstated the same way. Externally, walking away leaves CraftHaven to a rival — but a rival buyer suffers no cannibalization, which is precisely why the asset is worth more to them than to us; losing this auction is not a loss.
>
> Next steps. Within 30 days, counter at $469 million with a scanner-verified earn-out on non-cannibalized volume. In parallel, commission the same scanner analysis for the two other craft targets in the pipeline — the panel has been flattering all of them.

---

**Partner answer (Pyramid):**

> **We recommend Brewhalla does not close at $580 million — the acquisition is worth $469 million, and a quarter of what we would be buying is our own customers.**
