**Profitability · Прецизионная оптика · Hard · Trap · ~38 min · naive #5 · gen F**
*Registry: The Hunt for Red Optics*

**Type · Прецизионная оптика · F6 · Ловушка #5 (attributing a problem to where it is DETECTED) · Depth: STRONG**
Difficulty: Hard · Prototype: производитель оптических покрытий · IO: Industrials — прецизионное производство, yield · Layers: multi-insight ×2, hypothesis-update
cases.prompt_md: **Narvellis Optics** makes multi-layer coated optics. The production director shows a chart: defect rate rises with batch size. He proposes halving the batches. Do you agree?

exhibits.title: SCATTER — defect rate vs batch size by run
Defects attributed to the coating layer
triggers: where do the defects come from

exhibits.title: MEMO — line economics
exhibits.body_md:
> Chamber setup per run is **$96,000**: two days of pump-down and calibration. The cost is **lost chamber capacity**, and it arises **per run**, not per unit.
> Chamber capacity caps a run at **3,200** blanks; both lines share the chamber. Run size follows the order.
> Blank cost $310 · premium price (7–8 layers) $1,450 · standard price (3–5 layers) $620.
> Volumes: premium 96,000 units/year, standard 240,000 units/year.

steps.label: Framework (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: How would you assess the proposal to shrink the batches?
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) hypothesis first; (2) at least 3 MECE buckets; (3) the cause of the defects questioned, not the correlation alone; (4) a closing question.

steps.label: Naive screen (2 min)
steps.candidate_md: What does the scatter say?
steps.interviewer_md: **Answer: defects rise monotonically with batch size, 0.75% → 2.00%** → "shrink the batches". Trap #5: defects are **detected** by batch but **created** by passes.

steps.label: Hypothesis-update (2 min)
steps.candidate_md: Before opening Exhibit 2 — what do you expect?
steps.interviewer_md: Strong hypothesis: "a large batch is a different product, not a different process". Weak: "in a large batch a defect has time to propagate".

steps.label: Layer 1: attribution (5 min)
steps.candidate_md: Attribute the defects to layers.
steps.interviewer_md: **Answer: defects per 1,000 unit-layers are EXACTLY 2.50 across all six runs.** Premium optics are ordered in volume and also carry more layers: **batch size is a proxy, layers are the driver.** The process is in control.
steps.produces: брак на 1,000 unit-layers — РОВНО 2.50 на всех шести прогонах

steps.label: MAIN CALCULATION (6 min) — core
steps.candidate_md: Work out the effect of halving the batch on the premium line.
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Defects = units × layers × 0.0025 — independent of batch size:
          96,000 × 8 × 0.0025 = 1,920 units at any batch size
Only setup changes: 30 runs → 60, i.e. +30 × $96,000 = $2,880,000

Batch 3,200: profit $103,776,000
Batch 1,600: profit $100,896,000
```
**Answer: halving the batch DESTROYS $2,880,000 a year and saves not one blank.**
steps.produces: уменьшение партии УНИЧТОЖАЕТ $2,880,000/год и не спасает ни одной заготовки

steps.label: Layer 2: the defects are priced in (5 min)
steps.candidate_md: So is premium at 8 layers unprofitable?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
             Units    Layers  Defect %       Profit      $/unit
Premium      96,000     8     2.00%  $103,776,000   $1,081.00
Standard    240,000     4     1.00%   $65,712,000     $273.80
```
**Answer: premium is defective twice as often — exactly the ratio of layers — and earns four times as much per unit.** The extra defects are real and **already in the price**. The answer is neither "cut batches" nor "cut premium" but **shift the mix**: moving 24,000 units of capacity is worth **+$19,372,800/year** (full restatement of both lines: new volumes → new defects → new run count → new setup).
steps.produces: премиум бракуется вдвое чаще — ровно отношение слоёв — но зарабатывает вчетверо больш

steps.label: Sensitivity (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: At what defect rate would shrinking the batch pay off?
steps.produces: штраф ОДИН И ТОТ ЖЕ при любой ставке — партия не влияет на брак вообще. Порог не суще

steps.label: Synthesis (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: Your recommendation.
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) conclusion first ("leave the batches, shift the mix"); (2) at least 2 figures; (3) at least 2 risks (internal: chamber capacity for premium; external: premium optics demand, competitors); (4) at least 1 time-bound next step.

cases.title: Cable Guy Ropes
cases.header_md:
## Case 143 — Cable Guy Ropes

> **ПЛАШКА** 
> **Тип:** Pricing · **Индустрия:** Морской мооринг · **Формат:** F1  
> **Difficulty:** 🔴 Hard · **Depth:** 🔥 STRONG · **Соответствие:** OK  
> **T/C:** Trap · **Naive:** #4 · **Время:** ~38 min  
> **Экспонаты (3):** bridge — BRIDGE — от прайса к реализации, на линию; table — Ресурс — что клиент на самом деле покупает; memo — MEMO — экономика грейдов  
> **Reveal:** auto, on_request
> **optimal_entry:** 2  

**Pricing · Морской мооринг · Hard · Trap · ~38 min · naive #4 · gen F**
*Registry: Cable Guy Ropes*

**Type · Морской мооринг · F1 · Ловушка #4 (reading realised price off the discount schedule) · Depth: STRONG**
Difficulty: Hard · Prototype: производитель offshore-канатов · IO: Industrials — оборудование с ресурсом, TCO · Layers: multi-insight ×2, open-drive
cases.prompt_md: **Halbrent Marine** makes mooring lines for offshore platforms, 1,800 lines a year. The commercial director says discounting has got out of hand and wants the grid tightened. Where would you start?

exhibits.title: BRIDGE — from list price to realisation, per line
exhibits.body_md:
```
List price (mix-weighted)     $44,000.00  ->  $44,000.00
Volume discount               −$3,360.00  ->  $40,640.00
Term/framework rebate         −$2,100.00  ->  $38,540.00
Freight allowance               −$980.00  ->  $37,560.00
Early-replacement credit      −$4,620.00  ->  $32,940.00   <-- realisation
```
*Total leakage $11,060.00 per line on a list price of $44,000.00.*

exhibits.title: Service life — what the customer is actually buying
exhibits.body_md:
| Grade | Units | Rated cycles | Achieved | Shortfall | Credit/line |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Grade A (8-strand) | 600 | 2,400 | 2,400 | 0 | $0.00 |
| Grade B (12-strand) | 600 | 3,000 | 3,000 | 0 | $0.00 |
| **Grade C (HMPE blend)** | 600 | 4,200 | **2,940** | **1,260** | **$13,860.00** |

*Contractual credit: **$11.00** for each cycle short of the rating.*
*$8,316,000 / 1,800 lines = **$4,620.00** — exactly the bridge line.*

exhibits.title: MEMO — grade economics
exhibits.body_md:
> List: Grade A $38,000 · Grade B $42,000 · **Grade C $52,000**
> Cost: Grade A $24,000 · Grade B $27,500 · **Grade C $34,800**
> Volume + term + freight = **$6,440** per line on **every** grade.
> Grade C is the only grade certified for deepwater fields. Operators take the whole spread from one supplier: an attachment to C pulls **180** lines of A and **300** lines of B.

steps.label: Framework (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: How would you approach the price leakage?
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) hypothesis first; (2) at least 3 MECE buckets; (3) the nature of each bridge line questioned, not its size alone; (4) a closing question.

steps.label: Naive screen (2 min)
steps.candidate_md: Which line would you start with?
steps.interviewer_md: **Answer: the early-replacement credit, $4,620 — the largest** → "claw that back first". Trap #4.

steps.label: Layer 1: this is not a discount (5 min)
steps.candidate_md: Where does that line come from?
steps.interviewer_md: **Answer: it is a WARRANTY PAYMENT.** $11.00 per cycle short; A and B hit their rating exactly, and the entire shortfall sits in Grade C. **It cannot be "tightened": it is triggered by rope failure, not by sales policy.**

steps.label: MAIN CALCULATION (6 min) — core
steps.candidate_md: Work out profit by grade.
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Grade A: (38,000 − 6,440) − 24,000 = $7,560/line × 600 =  $4,536,000
Grade B: (42,000 − 6,440) − 27,500 = $8,060/line × 600 =  $4,836,000
Grade C: (52,000 − 6,440 − 13,860) − 34,800 = −$3,100 × 600 = −$1,860,000
                                                    TOTAL   $7,512,000
```
**Answer: the grade with the HIGHEST list price ($52,000) is the only loss-making one.** The premium price hides that C is sold below its true cost to serve.
steps.produces: грейд с САМЫМ ВЫСОКИМ прайсом ($52,000) — единственный убыточный

steps.label: Layer 2: dropping C is not an option either (5 min)
steps.candidate_md: So should Grade C be withdrawn?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Dropping C: we stop losing $1,860,000
            we lose pull-through 180×$7,560 + 300×$8,060 = $3,778,800
            net −$1,918,800 → KEEP
```
**Answer: withdrawal destroys $1,918,800 a year.** The action is neither "squeeze discounts" nor "kill the grade" but **fix the rope's service life**.

steps.label: The fix (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: What would the fix cost?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
HMPE re-spec + requalification: capex $5,200,000
Shortfall 1,260 → 0, net price $31,700 → $45,560
Grade C: −$1,860,000 → +$6,456,000 (swing $8,316,000)
Payback 0.63 years
```

steps.label: Sensitivity (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: How far does service life have to rise for C to break even?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Breakeven shortfall = ($52,000 − $6,440 − $34,800)/$11.00 = 978.18 cycles
→ achieved must exceed 3,221.82 cycles
@2,940 (today) → −$1,860,000    @3,221.82 → $0.00    @4,200 → +$6,456,000
```
**Answer: 3,221.82 cycles — the grade needs +281.82 cycles, not the whole 1,260 shortfall.**
steps.produces: 3,221.82 цикла — грейду нужно +281.82 цикла, а не весь недобор в 1,260

steps.label: Synthesis (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: Your recommendation.
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) conclusion first ("leave the grid, fund the re-spec"); (2) at least 2 figures; (3) at least 2 risks (internal: requalification lead time; external/regulatory: class certification for deepwater operations, HMPE price); (4) at least 1 time-bound next step.

cases.title: A Fish Called Wander
cases.header_md:
## Case 144 — A Fish Called Wander

> **ПЛАШКА** 
> **Тип:** Growth Strategy · **Индустрия:** Аквакультура · **Формат:** F6  
> **Difficulty:** 🔴 Hard · **Depth:** 🔥 STRONG · **Соответствие:** OK  
> **T/C:** Trap · **Naive:** #1 · **Время:** ~40 min  
> **Экспонаты (3):** cohort — COHORT-КРИВАЯ — биомасса на убое по поколени; table — Конверсия корма и сортность; memo — MEMO — прочие параметры  
> **Reveal:** auto, on_request
> **optimal_entry:** 2  

**Growth Strategy · Аквакультура · Hard · Trap · ~40 min · naive #1 · gen F**
*Registry: A Fish Called Wander*

**Type · Аквакультура · F6 · Ловушка #1 (headline volume growth read as business growth) · Depth: STRONG**
Difficulty: Hard · Prototype: норвежский лососевый фермер · IO: Agriculture/Protein — FCR как драйвер · Layers: multi-insight ×2, hypothesis-update
cases.prompt_md: **Thessix Aquaculture** farms salmon across six sites. Harvest biomass is up 57% over four years. The board wants to stock more smolt. Do you agree?

exhibits.title: COHORT CURVE — harvest biomass by smolt generation
Feed conversion and grade
triggers: ask about the cost of growth

exhibits.title: MEMO — other parameters
exhibits.body_md:
> Feed **$1.85/kg** · smolt **$1.30 each** · fixed cost per cycle across the whole estate **$18,000,000** (licences, moorings, crews).
> Six sites. A seventh site adds **$3,000,000** per cycle ($18,000,000 / 6).

steps.label: Framework (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: How would you assess the growth programme?
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) hypothesis first; (2) at least 3 MECE buckets; (3) an explicit distinction between total and marginal effect; (4) a closing question.

steps.label: Naive screen (2 min)
steps.candidate_md: What does the curve say?
steps.interviewer_md: **Answer: biomass +57%, total profit rising every year** → "the programme works, stock more". Trap #1.
steps.produces: биомасса +57%, совокупная прибыль растёт каждый год

steps.label: Hypothesis-update (2 min)
steps.candidate_md: Before opening Exhibit 2 — what do you expect?
steps.interviewer_md: Strong hypothesis: "density has a price — either feed or quality". Weak: "volume is up, so the economics are the same".

steps.label: Layer 1: the price of density (5 min)
steps.candidate_md: What is happening to conversion and quality?
steps.interviewer_md: **Answer: FCR 1.20 → 1.40, mortality 8% → 14%, superior share 95% → 65%.** Effective price falls $7.26 → $6.42/kg while volume rises. Density costs both feed and price.

steps.label: MAIN CALCULATION (6 min) — core
steps.candidate_md: Work out the marginal contribution of each generation.
steps.interviewer_md:
```
G-2021 → G-2022  +2,400t  +$6,852,000
G-2022 → G-2023  +2,400t  +$5,736,000
G-2023 → G-2024  +2,400t  +$1,260,000
G-2024 → G-2025  +2,400t    −$528,000   ← crossed zero
```
**Answer: the last generation DESTROYED $528,000.** Total profit is still rising ($74,532,000) — carried by the early generations, and that is the figure the programme reports on. **Growth stopped paying one generation ago, and the headline hides it.**

steps.label: Layer 2: rolling back is not the answer either (5 min)
steps.candidate_md: So should they roll back to the G-2024 level?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Rolling back: profit $74,532,000 → $75,060,000 = +$528,000
But it gives up 2,400t of volume and $8,688,000 of revenue for $528,000. That is treating the symptom.

The real lever is DENSITY, not volume:
the same 6,600 thousand smolt across a SEVENTH site restores G-2021 density
  FCR 1.40 → 1.20 · superior 65% → 95% · price $6.42 → $7.26/kg
  profit $74,532,000 → $103,476,000 on cycle capex of $3,000,000
```
**Answer: the seventh site adds $28,944,000. The constraint was never smolt, it was biomass per site.**
steps.produces: седьмой участок добавляет $28,944,000. Ограничение было не в мальке, а в биомассе на

steps.label: Sensitivity (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: At what superior share would G-2025 have broken even?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Breakeven eff. price at G-2025 volume = $6.4400/kg
→ superior* = 65.71% (observed 65.00%)
@65.00% → −$528,000    @65.71% → $0.00    @75.00% → +$6,864,000
```
**Answer: 65.71% — the generation falls 0.71 pp short.**

steps.label: Synthesis (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: Your recommendation.
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) conclusion first ("do not stock more on the current sites; open a seventh"); (2) at least 2 figures; (3) at least 2 risks (internal: time to bring a site on line, biosecurity; external/regulatory: MAB licence, a lice outbreak, feed price); (4) at least 1 time-bound next step.

cases.title: Foam Alone
cases.header_md:
## Case 145 — Foam Alone

> **ПЛАШКА** 
> **Тип:** Profitability · **Индустрия:** Матрасы DTC · **Формат:** F5  
> **Difficulty:** 🟡 Medium · **Depth:** ⚠️ STANDARD · **Соответствие:** OK  
> **T/C:** Trap · **Naive:** #6 · **Время:** ~30 min  
> **Экспонаты (2):** bar — STACKED BAR — продано и возвращено по канала; bridge — Экономика каналов и стоимость возврата  
> **Reveal:** auto, on_request
> **optimal_entry:** 2  

**Profitability · Матрасы DTC · Medium · Trap · ~30 min · naive #6 · gen F**
*Registry: Foam Alone*

**Type · Матрасы DTC · F5 · Ловушка #6 (fixing the channel with the biggest visible loss driver) · Depth: STANDARD**
Difficulty: Medium · Prototype: DTC-производитель матрасов · IO: Consumer/Retail — возвраты в trial-окне · Layers: brainstorm
cases.prompt_md: **Lattimore Bedding** sells mattresses direct, 100,000 units a year across four channels, with a trial period and free returns. The CFO proposes exiting the marketplace: "that is where the returns come from". Do you agree?

exhibits.title: STACKED BAR — sold and returned by channel
Channel economics and the cost of a return
triggers: what happens to a returned unit
exhibits.body_md:
| Channel | Net price | CAC | **CM on a kept unit** | **CM on a returned unit** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Own site | $1,180.00 | $310.00 | $389.00 | −$700.00 |
| **Marketplace** | $1,003.00 | **$95.00** | **$427.00** | **−$485.00** |
| Retail partner | $826.00 | $40.00 | $305.00 | −$430.00 |
| Wholesale | $590.00 | $0.00 | $109.00 | −$390.00 |

*Cost of goods $395 · outbound delivery $86 · return handling $145 · a returned mattress cannot be sold as new: open-box salvage **$236**.*

steps.label: Framework (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: How would you decide whether to exit a channel?
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) hypothesis first; (2) at least 3 MECE buckets; (3) the channel's contribution questioned, not the return rate alone; (4) a closing question.

steps.label: Naive screen (2 min)
steps.candidate_md: What does the chart say?
steps.interviewer_md: **Answer: Marketplace returns the most — 4,200 units at a 15.00% rate** → "exit". Trap #6.
steps.produces: Marketplace возвращает больше всех — 4,200 юнитов при ставке 15.00%

steps.label: Layer 1: what a return costs (5 min)
steps.candidate_md: Work out the unit economics by channel.
steps.interviewer_md: **Answer: Marketplace has the HIGHEST CM on a kept unit — $427** — because CAC is $215 below the own site. And a return there is the cheapest of any channel (−$485 against −$700 on the own site) for the same reason.
steps.produces: у Marketplace САМЫЙ ВЫСОКИЙ CM удержанного юнита — $427

steps.label: MAIN CALCULATION (5 min) — core
steps.candidate_md: Work out channel contribution after returns.
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Own site       38,640×$389   + 3,360×(−$700) = $12,678,960
Marketplace    23,800×$427   + 4,200×(−$485) =  $8,125,600
Retail partner 17,280×$305   +   720×(−$430) =  $4,960,800
Wholesale      11,880×$109   +   120×(−$390) =  $1,248,120
                                        TOTAL $27,013,480
```
**Answer: exiting Marketplace DESTROYS $8,125,600 of contribution** — more than Retail partner and Wholesale combined. The channel worth discussing is Wholesale ($1,248,120 on 12,000 units).

steps.label: BRAINSTORM (5 min)
steps.candidate_md: A return costs $485 a unit and the channel still delivers $8.1M. What would you do about the returns?
steps.interviewer_md:
Pass requires ALL of: at least 6 ideas, at least 2 groups, both working on the $485/unit loss, none of them cutting the channel.
**Model set (8 ideas, 2 groups):**
> **A. Prevent the return (matching before purchase):** (1) a firmness test gated at checkout — ship the matched model, not the chosen one; (2) swap the comfort layer instead of returning the whole unit; (3) communicate the 30-day adjustment period before the trial clock starts.
> **B. Recover more value (after the return):** (4) a local open-box outlet above the current $236; (5) a hotel and charity channel for sanitised units; (6) break down to components — springs and foam back into production; (7) route the return to the nearest buyer rather than to the warehouse; (8) a restocking fee on marketplace orders placed outside the matching path.

steps.label: Sensitivity (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: At what return rate would exiting be justified?
steps.produces: 46.82% — каналу нужно вернуть на 31.82 пп больше, втрое от сегодняшнего. Наивный выво

steps.label: Synthesis (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: Your recommendation.
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) conclusion first ("keep the channel, work on the returns"); (2) at least 2 figures; (3) at least 2 risks (internal: complexity of a matching gate at checkout; external/regulatory: marketplace return rules, the consumer's right to withdraw); (4) at least 1 time-bound next step.

cases.title: The Spy Who Loved Meat
cases.header_md:
## Case 146 — The Spy Who Loved Meat

> **ПЛАШКА** 
> **Тип:** M&A · **Индустрия:** Мясопереработка · **Формат:** F5  
> **Difficulty:** 🟡 Medium · **Depth:** ⚠️ STANDARD · **Соответствие:** OK  
> **T/C:** Trap · **Naive:** #5 · **Время:** ~32 min  
> **Экспонаты (3):** table — Заголовочный P&L цели; table — На что раскладывается туша; memo — MEMO — расписание контрактов  
> **Reveal:** on_request
> **optimal_entry:** 2  

**M&A · Мясопереработка · Medium · Trap · ~32 min · naive #5 · gen F**
*Registry: The Spy Who Loved Meat*

**Type · Мясопереработка · F5 · Ловушка #5 (valuing a target on the metric the seller reports on) · Depth: STANDARD**
Difficulty: Medium · Prototype: региональный мясопереработчик · IO: Food processing — выход туши, cut mix · Layers: mental-math
cases.prompt_md: **Meatharbor Foods** is considering the purchase of **Brawnley Processing**, which runs 420,000 head a year. Ask = 6.5× EBITDA. Meatharbor funds bolt-ons up to 7.0×. Should they buy?

exhibits.title: Target headline P&L
exhibits.body_md:
| Measure | Value |
|---|---|
| Head per year | 420,000 |
| Carcass weight | 340 kg per head |
| **Blended carcass price** | **$3.05/kg** ← the seller's metric |
| Revenue | $435,540,000 |
| Livestock + processing | $325,920,000 |
| Overhead | $18,900,000 |
| **EBITDA** | **$90,720,000** |

*Ask = 6.5 × EBITDA = **$589,680,000**.*

exhibits.title: How the carcass breaks down
triggers: ask how the carcass is sold
exhibits.body_md:
| Cut | kg/carcass | $/kg | $/carcass | Pricing |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Primal (loin/rib) | 56 | $7.50 | $420.00 | **annual contract** |
| Middle cuts | 94 | $3.50 | $329.00 | **annual contract** |
| Forequarter | 102 | $2.00 | $204.00 | spot |
| Trim & grinding | 68 | $1.00 | $68.00 | spot |
| Offal & rendering | 20 | $0.80 | $16.00 | spot |
| **Total** | **340** | | **$1,037.00** | |

*$1,037.00 / 340 kg = **$3.05/kg** — it ties to the headline. But **72.23% of the value** ($749.00) sits on annual contracts.*

exhibits.title: MEMO — contract calendar
exhibits.body_md:
> (1) Both annual contracts are with two retail groups and **renew in 11 months**. They were signed in a drought year, when cattle were scarce and processors held pricing power.
> (2) The current market for equivalent primal supply is **$7.10/kg**. Middle cuts are $3.50/kg, unchanged. Cattle have got cheaper, three competitors have added kill capacity, and the premium is gone.
> (3) The livestock cost in the P&L is **already** at the current market. So are the spot cuts.

steps.label: Framework (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: How would you assess the deal?
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) hypothesis first; (2) at least 3 MECE buckets; (3) the durability of the EBITDA questioned, not the multiple alone; (4) a closing question.

steps.label: Naive screen (2 min)
steps.candidate_md: What does the price tell you?
steps.interviewer_md: **Answer: 6.5× against a 7.0× limit** → "buy, it is inside the range". Trap #5: valuing on the metric the seller reports.

steps.label: Layer 1: what the blend is made of (5 min)
steps.candidate_md: Break down the $3.05/kg.
steps.interviewer_md: **Answer: it ties exactly ($1,037.00/340), but 72.23% of the value sits on annual contracts** that renew in 11 months. Spot is already at market; the contracts are not.
steps.produces: сходится точно ($1,037.00/340), но 72.23% стоимости — на годовых контрактах

steps.label: MAIN CALCULATION (6 min) — core
steps.candidate_md: Work out EBITDA after renewal.
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Primal $7.50 → $7.10 (market), everything else unchanged
Carcass value $1,037.00 → $1,014.60 (−$22.40)
EBITDA $90,720,000 → $81,312,000 (−$9,408,000)

NAIVE  : 7.0 × today's EBITDA = $635,040,000; the ask of $589,680,000 is BELOW → BUY
CORRECT: 7.0 × post-renewal EBITDA = $569,184,000; the ask of $589,680,000 is ABOVE → PASS
```
**Answer: the ask exceeds the limit by $20,496,000**, and the contracts renew **inside the holding period**.

steps.label: Explain (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: Why was the blended price misleading?
steps.interviewer_md: **Model answer:** it averages cuts that are priced on fundamentally different terms. Spot already reflects the fall in the market; the contracts do not yet. The single figure hides that almost three quarters of the value is locked on terms that are expiring.

steps.label: Sensitivity (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: At what primal price does the deal work?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
p* where 7.0×EBITDA(p) = ask → $7.2245/kg
@$7.50 (contract) → headroom +$45,360,000 → BUY
@$7.2245          → $0.00 → tie
@$7.10 (market)   → −$20,496,000 → PASS
```
**Answer: $7.2245/kg.** The market would have to recover $0.1245 of the $0.40 it lost.

steps.label: Synthesis (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: Your recommendation.
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) conclusion first ("do not buy at $589.7M; bid no more than $569.2M"); (2) at least 2 figures; (3) at least 2 risks (internal: integration of kill capacity; external/regulatory: cattle prices, veterinary requirements, retail bargaining power); (4) at least 1 time-bound next step.

cases.title: Plough and Prejudice
cases.header_md:
## Case 147 — Plough and Prejudice

> **ПЛАШКА** 
> **Тип:** Market Entry · **Индустрия:** Сельхозтехника · **Формат:** F5  
> **Difficulty:** 🟡 Medium · **Depth:** ⚠️ STANDARD · **Соответствие:** OK  
> **T/C:** Trap · **Naive:** #4 · **Время:** ~30 min  
> **Экспонаты (3):** map — MAP — арабельные регионы; table — Кто на самом деле убирает урожай; table — Моточасы определяют цикл замены  
> **Reveal:** auto, on_request
> **optimal_entry:** 2  

**Market Entry · Сельхозтехника · Medium · Trap · ~30 min · naive #4 · gen F**
*Registry: Plough and Prejudice*

**Type · Сельхозтехника · F5 · Ловушка #4 (sizing a market from population without the usage constraint) · Depth: STANDARD**
Difficulty: Medium · Prototype: производитель комбайнов · IO: Industrials — парк-часы, utilisation · Layers: mental-math · *soft-trap: overstate*
cases.prompt_md: **Tillmarsh Equipment** wants to enter the UK combine harvester market. Business development sizes it at $804,000,000 a year. Check the estimate.

exhibits.title: MAP — arable regions
exhibits.body_md:
```
       .-''-.
      /  EA  \      East Anglia       7,200 farms   avg 186 ha
     |  ####  |     Lincolnshire      4,800 farms   avg 168 ha
     \  EM LN /     East Midlands     5,400 farms   avg 142 ha
      '-.YK.-'      Yorkshire         3,900 farms   avg 124 ha
        SB          Scottish Borders  2,700 farms   avg  96 ha
                                     TOTAL 24,000 farms
```
*Combine: $268,000. Replacement cycle 8 years.*

exhibits.title: Who actually cuts the crop
exhibits.body_md:
A combine is justified from roughly **220 ha**. Below that a farm hires a contractor.

| Region | Farms | Avg ha | Own a machine | Served by contractor |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| East Anglia | 7,200 | 186 | 1,584 | 5,616 |
| East Midlands | 5,400 | 142 | 594 | 4,806 |
| Lincolnshire | 4,800 | 168 | 960 | 3,840 |
| Yorkshire | 3,900 | 124 | 351 | 3,549 |
| Scottish Borders | 2,700 | 96 | 135 | 2,565 |
| **Total** | **24,000** | | **3,624** | **20,376** |

*There are **640** contractors, each running **3** machines = **1,920** machines.*

exhibits.title: Engine hours drive the replacement cycle
triggers: ask how hard they are worked
how long does a machine last
exhibits.body_md:
A combine is traded at roughly **4,000 engine hours**.

| Operator | Machines | Hours/year | **Years to replacement** | Units/year |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Farmer-owner | 3,624 | 125 | **32** | 113.25 |
| Contractor | 1,920 | 500 | **8** | 240.00 |
| **Total** | | | | **353.25** |

steps.label: Framework (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: How would you check the market estimate?
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) hypothesis first; (2) at least 3 MECE buckets; (3) the question of who the buyer is, not only how many there are; (4) a closing question.

steps.label: Naive calculation (2 min)
steps.candidate_md: Where does the $804M come from?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
24,000 farms / 8 years = 3,000 combines a year × $268,000 = $804,000,000
```
**Answer: $804,000,000.** Trap #4: market size taken from a population without the constraint that governs its use.

steps.label: Layer 1: who owns one (5 min)
steps.candidate_md: Are all 24,000 farms buyers?
steps.interviewer_md: **Answer: only 3,624.** A combine is justified from 220 ha, and the average holding in the target regions runs 96–186 ha. The other 20,376 hire a contractor; there are 640 contractors running a fleet of 1,920 machines.

steps.label: MAIN CALCULATION (5 min) — core
steps.candidate_md: Rebuild the demand.
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Replacement runs on ENGINE HOURS, not on the calendar:
  farmer     125 h/yr → 4,000/125 = 32 years → 3,624/32 = 113.25 units/yr
  contractor 500 h/yr → 4,000/500 =  8 years → 1,920/8  = 240.00 units/yr
                                                TOTAL     353.25 units/yr

NAIVE  : 3,000 units/yr = $804,000,000
CORRECT:   353.25 units/yr = $94,671,000
```
**Answer: the direction is the SAME (the market is real), the overstatement is 749.26%.**

steps.label: Explain (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: Why is the naive figure so far out?
steps.interviewer_md: **Model answer:** both errors push the same way. It counts all 24,000 farms as buyers when 3,624 own a machine. And it applies an 8-year cycle to farmers who, at 125 hours a year, replace once every **32** years. The contractors are the exception: their 1,920 machines generate 240 units a year, twice what 3,624 farmer-owners generate. **This is a contractor market, and the naive frame measures farmers.**

steps.label: Sensitivity (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: What contractor utilisation would justify $804M?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
h* = 6,014.06 h/yr — 12.03 times the actual
and 1.50 times the machine's entire life (4,000 h). UNREACHABLE.
@400 h → $81,807,000   @500 (today) → $94,671,000
@800 h → $133,263,000  @1,000 h → $158,991,000
```
**Answer: the naive figure is unreachable at any plausible utilisation. The DECISION (enter) is robust; the SIZE has to be rebuilt from scratch.**
steps.produces: наивная цифра недостижима ни при какой правдоподобной загрузке. Решение (входить) роб

steps.label: Synthesis (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: Your recommendation.
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) conclusion first ("enter, but on $94.7M rather than $804M, and with a contractor-facing product"); (2) at least 2 figures; (3) at least 2 risks (internal: a dealer and service network built for high utilisation; external/regulatory: subsidies, grain prices, competitors with established contractor relationships); (4) at least 1 time-bound next step.

cases.title: Rebel Without a Claim
cases.header_md:
## Case 148 — Rebel Without a Claim

> **ПЛАШКА** 
> **Тип:** Profitability · **Индустрия:** Страхование P&C · **Формат:** F5  
> **Difficulty:** 🟡 Medium · **Depth:** ⚠️ STANDARD · **Соответствие:** OK  
> **T/C:** Trap · **Naive:** #3 · **Время:** ~31 min  
> **Экспонаты (3):** cohort — Портфель по когортам андеррайтинга; pie — Развитие убытков — доля итога, заявленная к ; memo — MEMO — два рычага на столе  
> **Reveal:** on_request
> **optimal_entry:** 2  

**Profitability · Страхование P&C · Medium · Trap · ~31 min · naive #3 · gen F**
*Registry: Rebel Without a Claim*

**Type · Страхование P&C · F5 · Ловушка #3 (acting on an undeveloped cohort loss ratio) · Depth: STANDARD**
Difficulty: Medium · Prototype: моторный страховщик · IO: Insurance — loss ratio по когортам, развитие убытков · Layers: mental-math · *soft-trap: action*
cases.prompt_md: **Claimtide Insurance** runs a motor book. The reported loss ratio has fallen from 74.00% to 35.20% over four years. The board proposes growing aggressively. Do you agree?

exhibits.title: Loss development — share of ultimate reported by month
exhibits.body_md:
| Months of development | % of ultimate loss reported |
|---|---|
| 6 | 55% |
| 18 | 80% |
| 30 | 92% |
| 42 | 100% |

*Motor claims are reported with a lag: bodily injury settles over years.*

exhibits.title: MEMO — two levers on the table
exhibits.body_md:
> Expense ratio **26.00%** of earned premium. Combined = ultimate loss + expense.
> **Lever A (growth):** write **20%** more policies on current terms.
> **Lever B (mix):** the 2025 cohort is not homogeneous —

| Segment | Policies | Premium | Ultimate LR | Combined |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Telematics | 76,800 | $67,584,000 | **58.00%** | **84.00%** |
| Standard | 51,200 | $45,056,000 | **73.00%** | **99.00%** |

*Weighted ultimate = 64.00% — it ties to the 2025 cohort.*

steps.label: Framework (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: How would you assess the proposal to grow?
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) hypothesis first; (2) at least 3 MECE buckets; (3) the maturity of the cohorts questioned; (4) a closing question.

steps.label: Naive screen (2 min)
steps.candidate_md: What do the numbers say?
steps.interviewer_md: **Answer: LR 35.20% against 74.00%** → "underwriting has improved sharply, grow harder". Trap #3.

steps.label: Layer 1: loss development (5 min)
steps.candidate_md: Can a cohort at 6 months be compared with one at 42?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Ultimate LR = reported / development factor
  2022  74.00% / 100% = 74.00%      2024  54.40% / 80% = 68.00%
  2023  65.78% /  92% = 71.50%      2025  35.20% / 55% = 64.00%
```
**Answer: underwriting has improved by 10.00 points, not 38.80.** A cohort at 6 months has reported barely half of the losses still to come.
steps.produces: андеррайтинг улучшился на 10.00 пунктов, а не на 38.80

steps.label: MAIN CALCULATION (6 min) — core
steps.candidate_md: Compare the two levers.
steps.interviewer_md:
```
2025 base: $112,640,000 × (100% − 64.00% − 26.00%) = $11,264,000

Lever A (20% growth on the current mix): $13,516,800 → +$2,252,800
Lever B (standard book moved to telematics terms):
         $112,640,000 × (100% − 58.00% − 26.00%) = $18,022,400 → +$6,758,400
```
**Answer: both levers improve profit, but B delivers exactly 3.00 times more** — with no capital and no new exposure.
steps.produces: оба рычага улучшают прибыль, но B даёт ровно в 3.00 раза больше

steps.label: Explain (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: Why is growth the worse choice?
steps.interviewer_md: **Model answer:** growing on the current mix scales the weaker half as well. 40% of the new premium lands in the standard book at a combined ratio of **99.00%** — a margin of 1.00 pp against 16.00 pp on telematics. Growth does not fix the mix, it replicates it.

steps.label: Sensitivity (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: What conversion share would match the growth programme?
steps.produces: треть портфеля равна всей 20%-й программе роста

steps.label: Synthesis (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: Your recommendation.
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) conclusion first ("do not grow on current terms; move the standard book onto telematics terms"); (2) at least 2 figures; (3) at least 2 risks (internal: speed of conversion, churn as terms tighten; external/regulatory: supervision of telematics pricing, data privacy); (4) at least 1 time-bound next step.

cases.title: The Bourne Inventory
cases.header_md:
## Case 149 — The Bourne Inventory

> **ПЛАШКА** 
> **Тип:** Cost Reduction · **Индустрия:** Промдистрибуция · **Формат:** F5  
> **Difficulty:** 🟢 Easy · **Depth:** ○ LIGHT · **Соответствие:** OK  
> **T/C:** Trap · **Naive:** #2 · **Время:** ~24 min  
> **Экспонаты (2):** table — Запас по полосам SKU; memo — MEMO — что каждая полоса реально отдаст  
> **Reveal:** on_request
> **optimal_entry:** 2  

**Cost Reduction · Промдистрибуция · Easy · Trap · ~24 min · naive #2 · gen F**
*Registry: The Bourne Inventory*

**Type · Промдистрибуция · F5 · Ловушка #2 (sizing a saving from an average, ignoring the distribution) · Depth: LIGHT**
Difficulty: Easy · Prototype: дистрибьютор промышленных комплектующих · IO: Distribution — оборачиваемость SKU · Layers: mental-math · *soft-trap: overstate*
cases.prompt_md: **Invenhaus Supply** holds $83,600,000 of inventory against annual COGS of $209,000,000. The operations director says: "the book turns 2.50 times, the industry benchmark is 2.75 — let us release working capital". What is that worth?

exhibits.title: MEMO — what each band would actually give up
triggers: how much comes back as cash
exhibits.body_md:
| Band | Inventory | **Reducible** | **Recovery on disposal** | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A — fast | $14,400,000 | **0%** | — | already 8.00 turns; cutting means out-of-stock |
| B — steady | $21,000,000 | 5% | 100% | safety stock trimmed without hurting service |
| C — slow | $19,200,000 | 10% | 100% | consolidation into regional hubs |
| D — dead | $29,000,000 | 8% | **35%** | only the still-saleable portion clears; the rest is obsolete |

steps.label: Framework (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: How would you size the release?
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) hypothesis first; (2) at least 3 MECE buckets; (3) the structure of the inventory questioned, not the average alone; (4) a closing question.

steps.label: Naive calculation + mental math (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: Work out the effect of reaching 2.75 turns, in your head.
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Required inventory = $209,000,000 / 2.75 = $76,000,000
Release = $83,600,000 − $76,000,000 = $7,600,000
Holding saved = × 22.00% = $1,672,000/year
```
**Answer: $1,672,000 a year.** Trap #2: a saving computed off the average, with no regard for the distribution.

steps.label: MAIN CALCULATION (5 min) — core
steps.candidate_md: Check how much of that is actually reducible.
steps.interviewer_md:
```
A: $14,400,000 × 0%  = $0          (cannot be cut — out-of-stock)
B: $21,000,000 × 5%  = $1,050,000
C: $19,200,000 × 10% = $1,920,000
D: $29,000,000 × 8%  = $2,320,000
                TOTAL  $5,290,000  reducible

Saving = $5,290,000 × 22.00% = $1,163,800/year
```
**Answer: the direction is the SAME (the money is real), the annual saving is overstated by 43.67%.**
steps.produces: направление ТО ЖЕ (деньги реальны), завышение годовой экономии 43.67%

steps.label: Second pass: the one-off cash (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: And how much cash does it bring in immediately?

steps.label: Explain (2 min)
steps.candidate_md: Why was the average turn misleading?
steps.interviewer_md: **Model answer:** 2.50 is a single figure laid over bands that differ by a factor of 20 (8.00 against 0.40). The fast bands are already optimal and cannot be cut; the dead bands can be cut but do not convert to cash at book value. The average hides both.

steps.label: Sensitivity (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: What if the dead stock could be cleared at a better price?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
The $1,163,800 annual saving does not depend on recovery — the stock leaves the warehouse either way.
Recovery only affects the one-off cash:
@20% → $3,434,000   @35% → $3,782,000   @60% → $4,362,000   @100% → $5,290,000
```
**Answer: even at 100% of book, the one-off cash is $5,290,000 against the naive $7,600,000. No threshold is printed: the constraint is on volume, not on price** — only $5,290,000 is reducible.
steps.produces: даже при 100% книги разовый кэш $5,290,000 против наивных $7,600,000. Порог не печата

steps.label: Synthesis (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: Your recommendation.
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) conclusion first ("a programme worth $1.16M a year and $3.78M once, and the 2.75 target is not reachable by trimming"); (2) at least 2 figures; (3) at least 2 risks (internal: out-of-stock risk from trimming B, the P&L hit from writing down D; external: demand for obsolete stock, supplier terms); (4) at least 1 time-bound next step.

cases.prompt_md:
**Vantrode Machines** proposes placing 240 new machines across four site types. The economics look clean. Should they launch?

*(Clean case: naive and correct agree — GO. The candidate's job is to NAME the hypotheses of a hidden reversal and CLOSE each one with a calculation, not to say "the numbers add up".)*

exhibits.title: Proposed placement
triggers: what does each site type earn
exhibits.body_md:
| Site type | Machines | Revenue/machine-day | Gross margin | Annual revenue |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Transport hubs | 60 | $42.00 | 58.00% | $919,800 |
| Office lobbies | 90 | $26.00 | 62.00% | $854,100 |
| Hospitals | 50 | $34.00 | 60.00% | $620,500 |
| Campuses | 40 | $30.00 | 61.00% | $438,000 |
| **Total** | **240** | | | **$2,832,400** |

*Machine $7,400 installed · servicing $2,600 per machine per year (restocking, cash collection, repair).*

exhibits.title: MEMO — the existing estate
triggers: ask about the machines we already have
exhibits.body_md:
> The existing estate is **310** machines at **$28.00** per machine-day and a gross margin of **60.00%**.
> Commercial's estimate: the new sites will take **4.00%** of the existing estate's revenue.

steps.label: Framework (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: How would you decide whether to launch?
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) hypothesis first; (2) at least 3 MECE buckets; (3) **the hypotheses of a possible reversal named explicitly**; (4) a closing question.

steps.label: Base case (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: Work out the base case.
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Revenue $2,832,400 · gross profit $1,702,506
Servicing 240 × $2,600 = $624,000
Annual profit $1,078,506
Capex 240 × $7,400 = $1,776,000 → payback ~1.65 years
```
**Answer: all four site types are profitable. Naive and correct AGREE: GO.**
steps.produces: все четыре типа точек прибыльны. Наив и correct СОВПАДАЮТ: GO

steps.label: Reversal hypothesis 1 (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: Is the weakest site type dragging the case down?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Campuses: $163,180 on 40 machines — POSITIVE
Without them: profit $915,326, capex $1,480,000, payback ~1.62 against ~1.65
```
**Answer: it neither drags nor carries. CLOSED by calculation.**
steps.produces: не тянет и не тащит. ЗАКРЫТА расчётом

steps.label: Reversal hypothesis 2 (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: What about cannibalising the existing estate?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Existing estate: 310 × $28.00 × 365 = $3,168,200
Losing 4.00% of revenue × 60.00% margin = $76,036.80
Project profit: $1,078,506 → $1,002,469.20, payback ~1.77
```
**Answer: cannibalisation costs 7.05% of the uplift — not a reversal. CLOSED.**
steps.produces: каннибализация стоит 7.05% прироста — не разворот. ЗАКРЫТА

steps.label: Reversal hypothesis 3 (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: And if servicing gets more expensive — new routes, vans, staff?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Stress $2,600 → $3,400 per machine per year (+30.77%):
  profit $1,078,506 → $886,506, payback ~2.00
  Transport hubs, offices, hospitals, campuses — ALL remain positive
```
**Answer: CLOSED.**

steps.label: Sensitivity (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: Where does the boundary actually lie?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Breakeven servicing = $1,702,506 / 240 = $7,093.775 per machine per year
(this is NOT $7,093.78 — the value sits on a half-cent; the control points are computed from the exact figure)
@$2,600 → $1,078,506   @$3,400 → $886,506   @$7,093.775 → $0.00   @$9,000 → −$457,494
```
**Answer: 172.84% of headroom on servicing cost.**

steps.label: Synthesis (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: Your recommendation.
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) a GO conclusion in the first sentence; (2) **an explicit statement that the absence of a reversal was tested** — three hypotheses run and closed; (3) at least 2 figures ($1,078,506/year, payback ~1.65, headroom 172.84%); (4) at least 2 risks (internal: restocking logistics as the estate grows; external/regulatory: site leases, regulation of vending in hospitals); (5) at least 1 time-bound next step.

exhibits.title: Where the volume sits — analyser-hours
exhibits.body_md:
| Platform | Analysers | Hours each | Utilisation | Tests/hour | Tests/year | Free hours |

steps.label: Framework (5 min)

steps.candidate_md: Work out the synergy on the deal thesis.

NAIVE                      $34,140,000        $307,260,000            BUY
What fits today            $21,248,500        $191,236,500       PASS (−$81,883,500)

cases.header_md:
## Case 152 — The Maltese Falconer

> **ПЛАШКА** 
> **Тип:** Profitability · **Индустрия:** Молочная переработка · **Формат:** F1  
> **Difficulty:** 🔴 Hard · **Depth:** 🔥 STRONG · **Соответствие:** OK  
> **T/C:** Trap-flip · **Naive:** — · **Время:** ~33 min  
> **Экспонаты (4):** flow — FLOW — куда идёт сырое молоко; table — Отчётный P&L по линиям; memo — MEMO — почему линия существует; memo — MEMO — альтернативная переработка излишка

> **optimal_entry:** 2  

**Profitability · Молочная переработка · Hard · Trap-flip · ~33 min · gen F**
*Registry: The Maltese Falconer*

**Type · Молочная переработка · F1 · Ловушка #9 (закрыть худшую по марже линию) · Depth: STRONG**
Difficulty: Hard · Prototype: региональный молочный завод · IO: Food processing — выход на тонну молока · Layers: 2
cases.prompt_md: **Marlhaven Dairy** processes 240,000 tonnes of raw milk a year across four lines. The milk powder line is showing a loss. Should it be closed?

exhibits.title: FLOW — where the raw milk goes
triggers: ask how the milk is split
exhibits.body_md:
```
   240,000 t raw milk
        |
        +---> Cheese           96,000 t  (40%)
        +---> Butter/cream     72,000 t  (30%)
        +---> Drinking milk    48,000 t  (20%)
        +---> Milk powder       24,000 t  (10%)
```

| Line | Milk, t | kg of output per t of milk | Price $/kg | Processing $/t of milk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cheese | 96,000 | 102 | $7.80 | $186.00 |
| Butter/cream | 72,000 | 118 | $5.40 | $124.00 |
| Drinking milk | 48,000 | 970 | $0.62 | $96.00 |
| Milk powder | 24,000 | 88 | $4.10 | $152.00 |

*Raw milk is $420.00/t. Yield is the physics of the product, not a choice.*

exhibits.title: MEMO — why the line exists
triggers: ask what happens to the milk
exhibits.body_md:
> 1. Milk arrives under an **intake contract**: farmers deliver what the herd gives and the plant is obliged to take all of it. The intake volume is not the plant's decision.
> 2. Cheese and butter run at the **equipment ceiling** every day. Neither will take an extra tonne without new capacity.
> 3. Drinking milk is capped by **retail orders**, not by the plant.
> 4. Milk powder is the **balancing line**: it takes whatever the other three do not. Its alternative is not another product but **disposal** at $38.00/t (tanker, treatment, effluent charge).
>
> Ceilings: cheese 96,000 t · butter 72,000 t · drinking 48,000 t = 216,000 t of the 240,000 t intake.

exhibits.title: MEMO — an alternative use for the surplus
exhibits.body_md:
> The same surplus can be made into **protein concentrate**: yield **64** kg/t (below the 88 of milk powder), price **$7.90**/kg, processing **$214.00**/t of milk.
> Installation: capex **$6,000,000**, over 5 years.

steps.label: Framework (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: How would you decide the fate of the milk powder line?
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) hypothesis first; (2) at least 3 MECE buckets; (3) the question of what happens to the milk on closure raised; (4) a closing question.

steps.label: Naive reading (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: What does the reported P&L say?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Milk powder: −$211.20 per tonne of milk — the only negative line
Naive #9: close it, recover $5,068,800
```
**Answer: this is the naive read. It assumes the milk need not be bought.**
steps.produces: это наив. Он предполагает, что молоко можно не покупать

steps.label: CORE: the unavoidable cost (7 min)
steps.candidate_md: Check what actually changes on closure.
steps.interviewer_md:
```
The report charges $420.00/t to the line:
  $8,659,200 − $10,080,000 − $3,648,000 = −$5,068,800

But the intake is take-or-pay: the $10,080,000 is spent whatever the decision.
An unavoidable cost belongs to NEITHER side of the choice.

Value recovered (revenue − processing) : $5,011,200
Disposal avoided (24,000 t × $38.00)   :   $912,000
Effect of CLOSING                      : −$5,923,200
```
**Answer: closing DESTROYS $5,923,200 a year. The choice is not "milk powder or cheese" but "milk powder or the drain".**
steps.produces: закрытие РАЗРУШАЕТ $5,923,200/год. Выбор не «сухое молоко или сыр», а «сухое молоко и

steps.label: Layer 2: a better form of the outlet (6 min)
steps.candidate_md: Is keeping the line the whole answer?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
                        kg/t   $/kg   processing   recovered
Milk powder (today)       88   $4.10     $152.00    $5,011,200
Protein concentrate       64   $7.90     $214.00    $6,998,400

uplift $1,987,200 − capex $6,000,000 over 5 years = net $787,200/year
```
**Answer: no. The yield is LOWER (64 against 88), but the price is $3.80/kg higher. The reported P&L could not show this — it charges both options the same unavoidable $420/t.**
steps.produces: нет. Выход НИЖЕ (64 против 88), но цена выше на $3.80/кг. Отчётный P&L этого показать

steps.label: Threshold (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: How robust is the switch to concentrate?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
p* = $7.3875/kg exactly (NOT $7.39 — the value runs to four decimals)
  price $6.0000 → −$2,131,200 → stay
  price $7.3875 →          $0 → tie
  price $7.9000 →   +$787,200 → switch
  price $9.0000 → +$2,476,800 → switch
```
**Answer: the price would have to fall $0.5125/kg (6.49%) for the switch to stop paying. Milk powder remains the fallback either way.**
steps.produces: цена должна упасть на $0.5125/кг (6.49%), чтобы переход перестал окупаться. Сухое мол

steps.label: Recommendation (5 min)
steps.candidate_md: Your conclusion for the board.
steps.interviewer_md: Pass on the Pyramid: (1) conclusion first — do NOT close the line, move the surplus into concentrate; (2) at least 2 figures (closing destroys $5,923,200; the switch delivers $787,200 a year on 6.49% of headroom); (3) at least 2 risks — internal ($6,000,000 of capex and a new process to master) + external/regulatory (food approvals for protein concentrate, the terms of the intake contract); (4) an urgent next step.

**Cost Reduction · Водоканал · Hard · Trap-flip · ~33 min · gen F**
*Registry: Twelve Angry Pipes*

**Type · Водоканал · F1 · Ловушка #10 (атаковать крупнейшую абсолютную потерю) · Depth: STRONG**
Difficulty: Hard · Prototype: региональный водоканал · IO: Utilities — стоимость сбережения кубометра · Layers: 2
cases.prompt_md: **Kestwater Utilities** loses 9,800,000 m³ of water a year. The board has released budget for a leakage reduction programme. Which zone should it start with?

exhibits.title: What the losses are made of, and what a fix costs
exhibits.body_md:
| Zone | Mains bursts | Pressure/service pipes | Mains replacement |
|---|---|---|---|
| Harbour Reach | 3,360,000 | 840,000 | $27,200,000 |
| **Old Quarter** | 700,000 | **2,800,000** | $14,800,000 |
| Northfell | 1,120,000 | 280,000 | $20,800,000 |
| Meadowside | 560,000 | 140,000 | $12,000,000 |

*The components tie to the losses in Exhibit 1 zone by zone.*
*Mains replacement recovers **only** the bursts. Pressure and service pipes are addressed by **pressure management**: $1,450,000 per zone.*
*Water costs $0.94/m³ (avoidable treatment and pumping). Asset lives: mains 20 years, pressure scheme 10 years.*

exhibits.title: MEMO — how the schemes interact
triggers: ask if we can do both
exhibits.body_md: > Lowering pressure reduces more than pressure leakage: the **frequency of bursts** on the remaining pipes also falls, by **30%** in any zone where pressure has been regulated.

steps.label: Framework (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: How would you choose the zone?
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) hypothesis first; (2) at least 3 MECE buckets; (3) the COST of saving a cubic metre raised explicitly, not the volume lost alone; (4) a closing question.

steps.label: Naive choice (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: What does the map say?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Harbour Reach loses the most: 4,200,000 m³
Naive #10: start replacing mains there
```
**Answer: this is the naive read. Volume lost is not the saving available.**
steps.produces: это наив. Объём потерь ≠ доступная экономия

steps.label: CORE: cost per cubic metre saved (7 min)
steps.candidate_md: Work out the economics of the options.
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Zone            Option                 m³      Capex       Annual value  Annual cost      NET
Harbour Reach   mains replacement   3,360,000  $27,200,000    $3,158,400    $1,360,000  $1,798,400
Harbour Reach   pressure management   840,000   $1,450,000      $789,600      $145,000    $644,600
Old Quarter     mains replacement     700,000  $14,800,000      $658,000      $740,000    −$82,000
Old Quarter     pressure management 2,800,000   $1,450,000    $2,632,000      $145,000  $2,487,000
Northfell       mains replacement   1,120,000  $20,800,000    $1,052,800    $1,040,000     $12,800
Northfell       pressure management   280,000   $1,450,000      $263,200      $145,000    $118,200
Meadowside      mains replacement     560,000  $12,000,000      $526,400      $600,000    −$73,600
Meadowside      pressure management   140,000   $1,450,000      $131,600      $145,000    −$13,400
```
**Answer: the best option is Old Quarter, pressure management: $2,487,000 a year against $1,798,400 for the naive choice. Old Quarter loses LESS, but 80.00% of its losses are pressure-driven. Incidentally: two of the replacement programmes are loss-making outright.**
steps.produces: лучший вариант — Old Quarter, управление давлением: $2,487,000/год против $1,798,400

steps.label: Layer 2: the schemes are not independent (6 min)
steps.candidate_md: Can both programmes be approved on their standalone figures?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Harbour Reach, mains replacement standalone : $1,798,400
The same programme AFTER pressure management :   $850,880  (2,352,000 m³ instead of 3,360,000)

Both schemes, pressure first                 : $1,495,480
Both schemes, costed separately              : $2,443,000
```
**Answer: no. Approving both on standalone figures overstates the effect by $947,520 — the same water is counted twice. Pressure schemes are appraised FIRST, and the mains business case is rebuilt on what is left.**
steps.produces: нет. Утверждение обеих по отдельным цифрам завышает эффект на $947,520 — одна и та же

steps.label: Threshold (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: How robust is this to the price of water?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
v* = $2.1696/m³ (repeating, shown to 4 decimals)
  $0.4000/m³ → gap  $991,000 → pressure
  $0.9400/m³ → gap  $688,600 → pressure
  $2.1696/m³ → gap        $0 → tie
  $3.0000/m³ → gap −$465,000 → mains
```
**Answer: the pressure scheme wins BELOW $2.1696/m³. Above it the larger volume of the mains programme takes over (3,360,000 against 2,800,000). Water today is $0.94 — less than half the threshold, so the conclusion survives a doubling of the price.**
steps.produces: схема давления выигрывает НИЖЕ $2.1696/м³. Выше — побеждает больший объём магистралей

steps.label: Recommendation (5 min)
steps.candidate_md: Your conclusion for the board.
steps.interviewer_md: Pass on the Pyramid: (1) conclusion first — start with pressure management in Old Quarter; (2) at least 2 figures ($2,487,000 a year against $1,798,400; $947,520 of double counting if both programmes are approved); (3) at least 2 risks — internal (lower pressure may trigger complaints about flow on upper floors) + external/regulatory (minimum pressure standards and leakage targets); (4) an urgent next step.

triggers: ask what happens if we raise it
exhibits.body_md:
> 1. Raising the pass **20%** loses **15%** of holders.
> 2. Of the trips those riders made, the **peak ones do not disappear** — the commute happens anyway. They convert to singles at $2.40.
> 3. The **off-peak ones do disappear**: discretionary trips that happened only because the pass makes them feel free.
> 4. Peak capacity is at its limit: every peak trip above today's level requires a marginal car at $1.85.
> 5. A peak surcharge of **$0.50** on singles loses **4%** of peak riders.

steps.label: Framework (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: How would you decide what to do with the fares?
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) hypothesis first; (2) at least 3 MECE buckets; (3) the COST of serving each type raised, not the fare alone; (4) a closing question.

steps.label: Naive reading (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: What jumps out?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Monthly: $0.95 a trip against $2.40 for a single
Naive #8: "the pass is underpriced, put it up"
```
**Answer: this is the naive read. The fare is compared without the cost to serve.**
steps.produces: это наив. Тариф сравнивается без себестоимости

steps.label: Raising the pass: it WORKS (6 min)
steps.candidate_md: Work out the 20% increase.
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Fare $0.95 → $1.14, with 15% of holders leaving
  those who stay     : 22,950,000 trips at $1.14
  leavers, peak      :  1,215,000 convert to singles at $2.40
  leavers, off-peak  :  2,835,000 disappear

Change in contribution: +$4,052,700
```
**Answer: the lever works. But $1,761,750 of the gain is the leavers' peak trips repriced at $2.40; they need the same cars. What disappears is off-peak travel that cost $0.22.**
steps.produces: рычаг работает. Но $1,761,750 прироста — это пиковые поездки ушедших, переоценённые в

steps.label: CORE: price the constraint, not the discount (6 min)
steps.candidate_md: Is there a better lever?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
The peak is filled by SINGLES (70.00% of their trips), not by the pass (30.00%).

A $0.50 peak surcharge on singles, losing 4% of peak riders:
  12,096,000 peak trips stay × $0.50 = $6,048,000
     504,000 leave × $0.55 contribution =   $277,200
  NET                                    $5,770,800

NAIVE:  raise the pass          +$4,052,700
BETTER: peak surcharge          +$5,770,800
```
**Answer: TRAP-ACTION. Both levers improve contribution, but the naive one is $1,718,100 worse AND sheds 2,835,000 off-peak trips. It prices the discount instead of the constraint.**
steps.produces: TRAP-ACTION. Оба рычага улучшают вклад, но наивный хуже на $1,718,100 И сбрасывает 2,

steps.label: BRAINSTORM (6 min)
steps.candidate_md: Give at least 6 ideas, MECE-structured.
steps.interviewer_md:
Pass at 6 or more ideas in 2 or more groups, all working on the gap between $1.85 and $0.22:
```
A. SHIFT DEMAND OFF THE PEAK:
   1. An off-peak pass at a deeper discount — fills seats at $0.22
   2. Fare bands in the shoulders of the peak instead of a cliff edge
   3. Employer agreements to stagger shift starts in return for a bulk rate
B. CHARGE FOR THE PEAK:
   4. A peak surcharge on singles (the calculated lever, $5,770,800)
   5. Split passes into peak-inclusive and off-peak-only
   6. A daily cap so heavy off-peak use stays worthwhile
C. ADD PEAK CAPACITY:
   7. Short-turn services on the busiest section instead of full-route runs
   8. Crew rostered to the shape of the peak rather than in even shifts
```
**Answer: 8 ideas, 3 MECE groups.**

steps.label: Two different thresholds (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: How robust is the surcharge?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
SIGN threshold: the surcharge stays positive up to a 47.62% loss of peak riders
  4.00%  → +$5,770,800
 20.00%  → +$3,654,000
 47.62%  →           $0 → tie
 60.00%  → −$1,638,000

OVERTAKING threshold: the surcharge stops BEATING the pass at 16.99%
  4.00%  → $5,770,800 against $4,052,700 → surcharge
 10.00%  → $4,977,000 against $4,052,700 → surcharge
 16.99%  → $4,052,700 against $4,052,700 → tie
 25.00%  → $2,992,500 against $4,052,700 → the pass
```
**Answer: these are DIFFERENT questions — "when does the lever stop working" and "when does it stop being the best one". At the researched 4% the surcharge wins by $1,718,100; above 16.99% raising the pass is better.**
steps.produces: это РАЗНЫЕ вопросы — «когда рычаг перестаёт работать» и «когда он перестаёт быть лучш

steps.label: Recommendation (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: Your conclusion for the board.
steps.interviewer_md: Pass on the Pyramid: (1) conclusion first — introduce the peak surcharge, do not raise the pass; (2) at least 2 figures ($5,770,800 against $4,052,700; headroom to a 47.62% loss); (3) at least 2 risks — internal (ticketing and validator software must distinguish peak periods) + external/regulatory (municipal operator fares are approved, and the surcharge falls on those who cannot move their shift); (4) an urgent next step — measure elasticity before rollout, since the recommendation is conditional on it.

## Case 156 — The Big Sleeper

Difficulty: Medium · Prototype: оператор спальных поездов · IO: Rail — вагоно-дни на рейс · Layers: 1
cases.prompt_md: **Halcyon Rail** runs four overnight routes. The board wants to close the weakest and move the capacity to the strongest. Which one should go?

exhibits.title: SCATTER — load factor by route
triggers: ask how full the trains are

exhibits.title: What each departure ties up — carriage-days
triggers: how long is a set held
exhibits.body_md:
*A carriage-day costs **$450.00** (lease plus maintenance plus depot).*

| Route | Carriages/train | Days held per departure | Carriage-days/departure | Carriage-days/year |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Northline | 12 | 2 | 24 | 12,480 |
| Coastway | 9 | 1 | 9 | 3,285 |
| **Highland** | 15 | **4** | **60** | 12,480 |
| Lakes Run | 10 | 1 | **10** | 3,120 |
| **Total** | | | | **31,365** |

*Long routes hold a set for several days: one night out, a layover, one night back.*

exhibits.title: MEMO — fares and operating costs
exhibits.body_md:
| Route | Average fare per berth | Operating cost per departure |
|---|---|---|
| Northline | $185.00 | $21,000.00 |
| Coastway | $142.00 | $14,400.00 |
| Highland | $268.00 | $36,000.00 |
| Lakes Run | $160.00 | $16,000.00 |

*Operating cost is traction, crew, catering and track access for one departure. It excludes carriage-days, which are the charge for the fleet.*

exhibits.title: MEMO — marginal demand
triggers: ask how new departures would fill
exhibits.body_md: > Commercial plans additional overnight capacity at a marginal load factor of **55%** — new departures do not fill like established ones.

steps.label: Framework (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: How would you choose the route to close?
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) hypothesis first; (2) at least 3 MECE buckets; (3) the question of which asset is scarce; (4) a closing question.

steps.label: Naive choice (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: What does load factor say?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Lakes Run — 70.00% against Northline's 90.00%
Naive #11: cut Lakes Run, move the capacity to Northline
```
**Answer: this is the naive read. Load factor measures how full a train is, not what the fleet returns.**
steps.produces: это наив. Загрузка меряет заполнение поезда, а не отдачу флота

steps.label: CORE: contribution per carriage-day (7 min)
steps.candidate_md: Work out the return on the scarce asset.
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Route        Revenue       Operating     Fleet        Contribution  $/carriage-day
Northline    $20,779,200   $10,920,000   $5,616,000   $4,243,200        $340
Coastway      $7,463,520    $5,256,000   $1,478,250     $729,270        $222
Highland     $13,378,560    $7,488,000   $5,616,000     $274,560         $22
Lakes Run     $6,988,800    $4,992,000   $1,404,000     $592,800        $190
TOTAL                                                 $5,839,830

Load factor:   Northline > Coastway = Highland > Lakes Run
Carriage-day:  Northline > Coastway > Lakes Run > Highland
```
**Answer: the two rankings DIVERGE. Lakes Run is second on return to the asset, not the worst. The route to examine is Highland: 80% load factor looks healthy, but $22 a carriage-day, because it holds 15 carriages for 4 days (60 carriage-days against Lakes Run's 10).**
steps.produces: два ранжирования РАСХОДЯТСЯ. Lakes Run — второй по отдаче на актив, а не худший. Пров

steps.label: What the naive plan actually does (6 min)
steps.candidate_md: Work the redeployment through.
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Closing Lakes Run frees 3,120 carriage-days
Northline: 24 carriage-days per departure → 130 extra departures

But Northline leaves only 12,480 berth-nights unsold,
while 130 departures add 130 × 240 = 31,200 berth-nights — 2.50× the visible demand.
New berths fill at the MARGINAL load factor of 55%, not at 90%.

  17,160 berths × $185 = $3,174,600
  − operating $2,730,000 − fleet $1,404,000 = −$959,400

NET effect of the move: −$959,400 − $592,800 = −$1,552,200
```
**Answer: the naive plan destroys $1,552,200 a year.**

steps.label: Threshold (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: At what load factor would the redeployment pay?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
lf* = 81.8919% (repeating, shown to 4 decimals)
  55.00% → −$1,552,200 → destroys
  70.00% →   −$686,400 → destroys
  81.89% →           $0 → tie
  95.00% →   +$756,600 → pays
```
**Answer: 81.8919% is BELOW the route's overall 90% — which is exactly why the naive plan looks plausible. The question is whether 130 ADDITIONAL departures fill like established ones, when supply would exceed visible demand by 2.50×.**
steps.produces: 81.8919% НИЖЕ общих 90% маршрута — именно поэтому наивный план выглядит правдоподобно

steps.label: Recommendation (5 min)
steps.candidate_md: Your conclusion for the board.
steps.interviewer_md: Pass on the Pyramid: (1) conclusion first — keep Lakes Run, re-examine Highland; (2) at least 2 figures (Lakes Run $190 a carriage-day against Highland's $22; the naive move destroys $1,552,200); (3) at least 2 risks — internal (the 55% marginal load factor is a planning assumption and has to be tested) + external/regulatory (public service obligations on the routes and infrastructure access slots); (4) an urgent next step.

cases.prompt_md: **Grainhold Trading** is appraising the purchase of **Thrayven Grain**. The seller proposes a valuation on the best year. What is the company actually worth?

exhibits.title: MEMO — what drove the margin
exhibits.body_md:
> 1. Volume is stable: 2,400,000 → 2,760,000 t, **+15.00%** over five years, tracking the regional harvest and elevator capacity.
> 2. Margin per tonne is **NOT stable**. 2022–23 covered a drought in a competing export basin: spreads widened and the whole region earned an exceptional carry.
> 3. That basin returned to normal production in 2024. Margin has fallen two years running, and 2025 is close to the 2021 level.
> 4. Elevator capacity is **2,900,000 t**. The headroom for volume growth is nearly exhausted.

steps.label: Framework (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: How would you value Thrayven?
steps.interviewer_md: Pass requires ALL of: (1) hypothesis first; (2) at least 3 MECE buckets; (3) the durability of the earnings base raised explicitly; (4) a closing question.

steps.label: Naive valuation (3 min)
steps.candidate_md: What is the seller proposing?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Best year 2023: EBITDA $43,580,000
6.5 × $43,580,000 = $283,270,000
```
**Answer: this is naive #13 — valuing the peak of a cycle as if it were the norm.**
steps.produces: это наив #13 — оценка по пику цикла как по норме

steps.label: Separate the drivers (5 min)
steps.candidate_md: What moved — volume or margin?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Volume: 2,400,000 → 2,760,000 t, +15.00%, a steady climb
Margin: $7.20 → $14.60 → $21.40 → $11.70 → $8.40 — a hump
```
**Answer: the hump is in margin, not in volume. The 2023 peak was a drought in a competing basin, not a structural advantage.**
steps.produces: горб в марже, а не в объёме. Пик 2023 — засуха в конкурирующем бассейне, а не структу

steps.label: CORE: normalisation (6 min)
steps.candidate_md: Value it on a normal margin.
steps.interviewer_md:
```
Normal years: 2021, 2024, 2025
Margins $7.20 / $11.70 / $8.40 → average $9.10/t

Normalised EBITDA on 2025 volume:
  2,760,000 × $9.10 − $14,600,000 = $10,516,000
Valuation at 6.5×: $68,354,000

NAIVE $283,270,000 · CORRECT $68,354,000 · overstatement 314.42%
```
**Answer: the direction is the SAME — the business is worth buying — but the peak figure overstates the value more than fourfold.**
steps.produces: направление ТО ЖЕ — бизнес стоит покупать — но пиковая цифра завышает стоимость в чет

steps.label: Threshold (4 min)
steps.candidate_md: What would have to be true for the seller's price to hold?
steps.interviewer_md:
```
m* = $21.0797/t (repeating, shown to 4 decimals)
   $9.1000/t →  $68,354,000 → below the ask
  $11.7000/t → $114,998,000 → below the ask
  $21.0797/t → $283,270,000 → tie
  $21.4000/t → $289,016,000 → above the ask
```
**Answer: a margin of $21.0797/t FOREVER — $11.9797 above the normal average, a level reached once in five years at the height of a drought. No volume threshold is printed: even at full capacity of 2,900,000 t the normalised valuation is $76,635,000, still far below the ask.**
steps.produces: нужна маржа $21.0797/т НАВСЕГДА — на $11.9797 выше нормального среднего, уровень, дос

steps.label: Recommendation (5 min)
steps.candidate_md: Your conclusion for the investment committee.
steps.interviewer_md: Pass on the Pyramid: (1) conclusion first — buy, but not at $283,270,000; (2) at least 2 figures ($68,354,000 normalised valuation, overstatement 314.42%); (3) at least 2 risks — internal (elevators are near their ceiling and organic volume growth is exhausted) + external/regulatory (export duties and the weather in a competing basin, neither within the buyer's control); (4) an urgent next step.
